### Market Resolution

Check a market's resolution progress.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Call `fetchResolutions()` on an existing `PublicClient` or `SecureClient`.
> If needed, [create a Public Client](/getting-started/typescript#create-a-public-client) first.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const resolutions = await client.fetchResolutions({
>   conditionIds: [conditionId],
> });
>
> for (const resolution of resolutions) {
>   console.log(
>     resolution.status,
>     resolution.transactionHash,
>     resolution.logIndex,
>   );
> }
>
> // resolutions: Resolution[]
> ```
>
> Each row includes its `status` and `lastUpdatedAt`. `payouts` is present
> when published. No matching resolution returns an empty array.
>
> For UMA question lifecycle rows, `transactionHash` identifies the latest
> lifecycle transaction, while `logIndex` is the initial `RequestPrice` event's
> log index. They can belong to different transactions. Do not combine them as
> a log locator.
>
> This rule does not apply uniformly to every row. V2 condition-only rows can
> return `null` for both fields. CTF condition-resolution fallback rows instead
> carry the paired transaction and log index of the condition-resolution event.
>
> Settlement estimates use these optional fields on `Resolution`:
>
> | Field | Type |
> | - | - |
> | `expectedSettlementTime` | `IsoDateTimeString` or `undefined` |
> | `settlementTimeBasis` | `ResolutionSettlementTimeBasis` or `undefined` |
>
> `expectedSettlementTime` is an ISO datetime string in UTC. The fields are
> omitted when no estimate is available. Import `ResolutionSettlementTimeBasis`
> from `@polymarket/client` to interpret the estimate:
>
> | Enum member | Estimate |
> | - | - |
> | `ManagedProposalExpiration` | End of the managed UMA proposal's challenge window |
> | `ProposalExpiration` | End of the ordinary UMA proposal's challenge window |
> | `DvmRoundEstimate` | Earliest end of the UMA voting round the dispute can settle in |
> | `Liveness` | Proposal time plus the Polymarket v2 oracle's liveness window |

> [tab] Python
>
> Call `get_resolutions()` on an existing `AsyncPublicClient` or `AsyncSecureClient`.
> If needed, [create a Public Client](/getting-started/python#create-a-public-client) first.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> resolutions = await client.get_resolutions(condition_ids=[condition_id])
>
> for resolution in resolutions:
>     print(resolution.status, resolution.transaction_hash, resolution.log_index)
>
> # resolutions: tuple[Resolution, ...]
> ```
>
> Each row includes `status` and `last_updated_at`. `payouts` contains the published payouts when available. No matching resolution returns an empty tuple.
>
> For UMA question lifecycle rows, `transaction_hash` identifies the latest
> lifecycle transaction, while `log_index` is the initial `RequestPrice` event's
> log index. They can belong to different transactions. Do not combine them as
> a log locator.
>
> This rule does not apply uniformly to every row. V2 condition-only rows can
> return `None` for both fields. CTF condition-resolution fallback rows instead
> carry the paired transaction and log index of the condition-resolution event.
>
> Settlement estimates use these fields on `Resolution`:
>
> | Field | Type |
> | - | - |
> | `expected_settlement_time` | `datetime` or `None` |
> | `settlement_time_basis` | `ResolutionSettlementTimeBasis` or `None` |
>
> `expected_settlement_time` is a timezone-aware UTC `datetime`. The fields are
> `None` when no estimate is available. Import `ResolutionSettlementTimeBasis`
> from `polymarket` to interpret the estimate:
>
> | Enum member | Estimate |
> | - | - |
> | `MANAGED_PROPOSAL_EXPIRATION` | End of the managed UMA proposal's challenge window |
> | `PROPOSAL_EXPIRATION` | End of the ordinary UMA proposal's challenge window |
> | `DVM_ROUND_ESTIMATE` | Earliest end of the UMA voting round the dispute can settle in |
> | `LIVENESS` | Proposal time plus the Polymarket v2 oracle's liveness window |

> [tab] API
>
> Fetch resolution progress for the market:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl "https://data-api.polymarket.com/v2/resolutions?condition=$CONDITION_ID"
> ```
>
> Illustrative response (fields trimmed):
>
> > [accordion] Output: Resolutions
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > {
> >   "data": [
> >     {
> >       "condition_id": "0x02507350fc2b81c3af36c659a805adbda9b0a81e63a27b29cb273cdd7dbc072e",
> >       "status": "resolved",
> >       "transaction_hash": "0x1fc7a1df48dcac15859af515ebd77183c3487591181469a60dbf115b705f005a",
> >       "log_index": "170",
> >       "last_update_timestamp": "1785355919"
> >     }
> >   ]
> > }
> > ```
>
> `data` contains resolution rows with `status` and `last_update_timestamp`, or
> an empty list when no resolution matches. While a market waits on its oracle,
> a row can carry the settlement estimate fields described below.
>
> For UMA question lifecycle rows, `transaction_hash` identifies the latest
> lifecycle transaction, while `log_index` is the initial `RequestPrice` event's
> log index as a numeric string. They can belong to different transactions.
> Do not combine them as a log locator.
>
> V2 condition-only rows can return empty strings for both fields when provenance
> is unavailable. CTF condition-resolution fallback rows instead return the
> paired transaction and log index of the condition-resolution event.
>
> A row that is waiting on an oracle can carry `expected_settlement_time`
> (RFC3339 UTC) and `settlement_time_basis`. Both are omitted whenever no
> estimate applies, including settled markets and proposals under extended
> review.
>
> | `settlement_time_basis` | Row state | `expected_settlement_time` |
> | - | - | - |
> | `managed_proposal_expiration` | UMA proposal on the managed oracle, still in its challenge window | End of the challenge window |
> | `proposal_expiration` | UMA proposal on the ordinary oracle, still in its challenge window | End of the challenge window |
> | `dvm_round_estimate` | UMA proposal under dispute | Earliest end of the UMA voting round the dispute can settle in |
> | `liveness` | Proposal on Polymarket's v2 oracle | Proposal time plus its liveness window |

#### Settlement Estimates

Treat an estimate as the earliest time the market can settle, not as a
deadline. A disputed vote can roll into a later voting round, and a proposal's
liveness window can already have elapsed while it awaits finalization.

No estimate is available for settled markets, proposals under extended review,
or markets that are still initialized or active.

### Token Lookup

Find the market and outcome for a token, or list all tokens of a condition in
one read.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Call `fetchTokenReferences()` on an existing `PublicClient` or `SecureClient`.
> If needed, [create a Public Client](/getting-started/typescript#create-a-public-client) first.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const assetId =
>   "107505882767731489358349912513945399560393482969656700824895970500493757150417";
> const references = await client.fetchTokenReferences({ assetIds: [assetId] });
>
> for (const reference of references) {
>   console.log(reference.assetId, reference.outcome, reference.outcomeIndex);
> }
>
> // references: TokenReference[]
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: TokenReference\[]
> >
> > ```ts TokenReference Type theme={null}
> > type TokenReference = {
> >   assetId: ClobAssetId;
> >   conditionId: ConditionId;
> >   structuralConditionId: ConditionId | null;
> >   module: TokenModule;
> >   outcomeIndex: number;
> >   clobIndex: number | null;
> >   outcome: string | null;
> >   oppositeAssetId: ClobAssetId | null;
> >   resolved: boolean;
> >   finalPrice: DecimalString | null;
> >   title: string | null;
> >   marketSlug: string | null;
> >   closed: boolean | null;
> >   negRisk: boolean | null;
> >   negRiskMarketId: ConditionId | null;
> >   questionIndex: number | null;
> >   eventId: EventId | null;
> >   eventSlug: string | null;
> > };
> > ```
>
> `finalPrice` is the settled payout as a decimal string, or `null` when
> unavailable. Settlement data can take up to a minute to update.
>
> To look up a condition instead, supply only `conditionIds`:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const references = await client.fetchTokenReferences({
>   conditionIds: [conditionId],
> });
> ```
>
> Pass up to 50 `assetIds` or 10 `conditionIds`, not both. Results are not
> paginated. Unknown asset IDs are omitted.

> [tab] Python
>
> Call `get_token_references()` on an existing `AsyncPublicClient` or
> `AsyncSecureClient`. If needed,
> [create a Public Client](/getting-started/python#create-a-public-client) first.
> Sync clients expose the same method.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> asset_id = "107505882767731489358349912513945399560393482969656700824895970500493757150417"
> references = await client.get_token_references(asset_ids=[asset_id])
>
> for reference in references:
>     print(reference.asset_id, reference.outcome, reference.outcome_index)
>
> # references: tuple[TokenReference, ...]
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: TokenReference
> >
> > ```python TokenReference Type theme={null}
> > class TokenReference(BaseModel):
> >     asset_id: ClobAssetId
> >     condition_id: ConditionId
> >     structural_condition_id: ConditionId | None
> >     module: TokenModule
> >     outcome_index: int
> >     clob_index: int | None
> >     outcome: str | None
> >     opposite_asset_id: ClobAssetId | None
> >     resolved: bool
> >     final_price: Decimal | None
> >     title: str | None
> >     market_slug: str | None
> >     closed: bool | None
> >     neg_risk: bool | None
> >     neg_risk_market_id: ConditionId | None
> >     question_index: int | None
> >     event_id: EventId | None
> >     event_slug: str | None
> > ```
>
> `final_price` is the settled payout as a `Decimal`, or `None` when
> unavailable. Settlement data can take up to a minute to update.
>
> To look up a condition instead, supply only `condition_ids`:
>
> ```python theme={null}
> references = await client.get_token_references(condition_ids=[condition_id])
> ```
>
> Pass up to 50 `asset_ids` or 10 `condition_ids`, not both. Results are not
> paginated. Unknown asset IDs are omitted.

> [tab] API
>
> Look up tokens by ID:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl "https://data-api.polymarket.com/v2/tokens?token_id=$TOKEN_ID,$OTHER_TOKEN_ID"
> ```
>
> Example response:
>
> > [accordion] Output: Token References
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > {
> >   "data": [
> >     {
> >       "token_id": "123",
> >       "condition_id": "0x747dc809fb79e1b05be09c42d6179459a58de2ef3e40f02484a4e1260f741f75",
> >       "structural_condition_id": null,
> >       "module": "v1_ctf",
> >       "outcome_index": 1,
> >       "clob_index": 0,
> >       "outcome": "Yes",
> >       "opposite_token_id": "124",
> >       "resolved": true,
> >       "final_price": 0.5,
> >       "title": "Example Market",
> >       "market_slug": "example-market",
> >       "closed": true,
> >       "neg_risk": false,
> >       "neg_risk_market_id": null,
> >       "question_index": null,
> >       "event_id": 1234,
> >       "event_slug": "example-event"
> >     }
> >   ]
> > }
> > ```
>
> To list all tokens for a condition:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl "https://data-api.polymarket.com/v2/tokens?condition=$NEG_RISK_MARKET_ID"
> ```
>
> Use `token_id` (up to 50 IDs) or `condition` (up to 10 IDs), not both.
> Separate multiple IDs with commas. Results are not paginated. Unknown token
> IDs are omitted.

## Trader Leaderboard

Compare trader volume and profit and loss over a selected period.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Call `listTraderLeaderboard()` on a `PublicClient` or `SecureClient`.
> `window` defaults to one day, `category` to overall, and `sortBy` to PnL.
> Tied traders share a rank and the next rank skips.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { LeaderboardWindow, TraderLeaderboardSort } from "@polymarket/client";
>
> const pages = client.listTraderLeaderboard({
>   window: LeaderboardWindow.Day,
>   sortBy: TraderLeaderboardSort.Pnl,
>   pageSize: 1,
> });
>
> for await (const page of pages) {
>   // page.items: TraderLeaderboardEntry[]
> }
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: TraderLeaderboardEntry\[]
> >
> > ```ts TraderLeaderboardEntry Type theme={null}
> > type TraderLeaderboardEntry = {
> >   /** Competition rank; ties share a rank and the next rank skips. */
> >   rank: number;
> >   wallet: EvmAddress;
> >   /** PnL in USD for the selected window. */
> >   pnl: DecimalString;
> >   /** Both-sides traded volume in shares. */
> >   volume: DecimalString;
> >   userName: string | null;
> >   profileImage: string | null;
> >   xUsername: string | null;
> >   verified: boolean;
> > };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json TraderLeaderboardEntry Example theme={null}
> > [
> >   {
> >     "rank": 1,
> >     "wallet": "0xfe787d2da716d60e8acff57fb87eb13cd4d10319",
> >     "pnl": "372027.33333288063",
> >     "volume": "3036239.1641930016",
> >     "userName": "ferrariChampions2026",
> >     "verified": false
> >   }
> > ]
> > ```
>
> Call `fetchTraderLeaderboardStanding()` on a `PublicClient` or
> `SecureClient` to read one wallet's standing on both boards.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const standing = await client.fetchTraderLeaderboardStanding({
>   user: wallet,
>   window: LeaderboardWindow.Day,
> });
>
> // standing: TraderLeaderboardStanding | null
> ```
>
> When called on a `SecureClient`, `user` can be omitted and defaults to the
> authenticated account's wallet.
>
> > [accordion] Output: TraderLeaderboardStanding
> >
> > ```ts TraderLeaderboardStanding Type theme={null}
> > type TraderLeaderboardStanding = {
> >   wallet: EvmAddress;
> >   pnl: DecimalString;
> >   volume: DecimalString;
> >   pnlRank: number | null;
> >   volumeRank: number | null;
> >   userName: string | null;
> >   profileImage: string | null;
> >   xUsername: string | null;
> >   verified: boolean;
> > };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json TraderLeaderboardStanding Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "wallet": "0xfe787d2da716d60e8acff57fb87eb13cd4d10319",
> >   "pnl": "420711.02199365385",
> >   "volume": "3920263.4910460007",
> >   "pnlRank": 1,
> >   "volumeRank": 1,
> >   "userName": "ferrariChampions2026",
> >   "profileImage": null,
> >   "xUsername": null,
> >   "verified": false
> > }
> > ```
>
> A `null` rank means the wallet is unranked on that board.

## Biggest Winners

Compare individual winning positions by their profit at resolution.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Call `listBiggestWinners()` on a `PublicClient` or `SecureClient`.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { LeaderboardWindow } from "@polymarket/client";
>
> const pages = client.listBiggestWinners({
>   window: LeaderboardWindow.Day,
>   pageSize: 10,
> });
>
> for await (const page of pages) {
>   // page.items: BiggestWinner[]
> }
> ```
>
> `window` selects the resolution period. Each row is one position. Check
> `kind` before using `eventId`, which is `null` for Combos.

> [tab] Python
>
> Call `list_biggest_winners()` on an existing `AsyncPublicClient` or `AsyncSecureClient`.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> pages = client.list_biggest_winners(window="day", page_size=10)
>
> async for page in pages:
>     # page.items: tuple[MarketBiggestWinner | ComboBiggestWinner, ...]
>     pass
> ```
>
> `window` selects the resolution period. Each row is one winning position. Check `kind` before accessing market-specific fields. `MarketBiggestWinner` identifies the asset with `asset_id` and includes `event_id`. `ComboBiggestWinner` uses `position_id`.

> [tab] API
>
> List the largest wins resolved in the last day:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl "https://data-api.polymarket.com/v2/biggest-winners?time_period=day&limit=10"
> ```
>
> `data` contains one row per winning position. Continue with
> `pagination.next_cursor` as `cursor` until it is `null`.

## Builder Analytics

Evaluate the reach of a builder integration through its attributed trading
activity.

### Builder Leaderboard

Compare builders by attributed volume and active users.

> [tab] TypeScript
>

### Builder Volume

Track attributed builder volume and active users over time.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Call `fetchBuilderVolume()` on a `PublicClient` or `SecureClient`.
> `interval` picks the bucket width and `bucketLimit` counts the most recent
> complete buckets (at most 90); every builder active in a bucket gets one
> row.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { BuilderVolumeInterval } from "@polymarket/client";
>
> const builderVolume = await client.fetchBuilderVolume({
>   interval: BuilderVolumeInterval.Day,
>   bucketLimit: 1,
> });
>
> // builderVolume: BuilderVolumePoint[]
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: BuilderVolumePoint\[]
> >
> > ```ts BuilderVolumePoint Type theme={null}
> > type BuilderVolumePoint = {
> >   /** UTC start date of the volume bucket. */
> >   bucketDate: IsoCalendarDateString;
> >   /** Builder rank within this bucket. */
> >   rank: number;
> >   /** Display name; use `builderCode` as the stable identifier. */
> >   builderName: string;
> >   builderCode: BuilderCode;
> >   profileImage?: string;
> >   verified: boolean;
> >   /** Builder-attributed volume in shares for this bucket. */
> >   volume: DecimalString;
> >   activeUsers: number;
> > };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json BuilderVolumePoint Example theme={null}
> > [
> >   {
> >     "bucketDate": "2026-09-03",
> >     "rank": 1,
> >     "builderName": "betmoar",
> >     "builderCode": "0xceebf77a833b30520287ddd9478ff51abbdffa30aa90a8d655dba0e8a79ce0c1",
> >     "verified": true,
> >     "volume": "1990330.1396780002",
> >     "activeUsers": 150
> >   }
> > ]
> > ```

> [tab] Python
>
> Call `get_builder_volumes()` on an existing `AsyncPublicClient` or `AsyncSecureClient`.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> builder_volume = await client.get_builder_volumes(interval="day", bucket_limit=1)
>
> # builder_volume: tuple[BuilderVolumePoint, ...]
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: BuilderVolumePoint
> >
> > ```python BuilderVolumePoint Type theme={null}
> > class BuilderVolumePoint:
> >     rank: int
> >     builder_name: str
> >     builder_code: HexString
> >     profile_image: str | None
> >     verified: bool
> >     volume: Decimal
> >     active_users: int
> >     bucket_date: date
> > ```
> >
> > ```json BuilderVolumePoint Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "rank": 1,
> >   "builder_name": "betmoar",
> >   "builder_code": "0xceebf77a833b30520287ddd9478ff51abbdffa30aa90a8d655dba0e8a79ce0c1",
> >   "profile_image": "https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/betmoar_2.png",
> >   "verified": true,
> >   "volume": "3419926.8151110006",
> >   "active_users": 165,
> >   "bucket_date": "2026-09-08"
> > }
> > ```
>
> The result is a tuple of calendar buckets. `bucket_limit` counts dates, not rows, and accepts at most 90. Each active builder has a row for that date. `volume` is in shares.

> [tab] API

# Real-Time Data
Source: https://docs.polymarket.com/market-data/realtime-data

Keep market data current with Polymarket's real-time feeds.

Use Polymarket's real-time feeds to react as market conditions and related data
change. They keep the public market data your application depends on current
without repeated polling. For authenticated order and trade updates, see
[Real-Time Order Updates](/trading/realtime-order-updates).

## Market Stream

Use the market stream to keep your application in sync with changes to a
market's order book and trading state.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> The unified SDK uses `assetId` for an outcome's trading identifier: a token
> ID for a CTF market or a position ID for a Polymarket Protocol V2 market.
> Use the identifier exposed for that outcome.
>
> Given a `PublicClient` or `SecureClient`, subscribe to the `market` topic with one or
> more outcome IDs:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const assetId = "<asset_id>";
>
> const stream = await client.subscribe([
>   {
>     topic: "market",
>     assetIds: [assetId],
>   },
> ]);
>
> for await (const event of stream) {
>   switch (event.type) {
>     case "book":
>       // event: MarketBookEvent
>       break;
>     case "price_change":
>       // event: MarketPriceChangeEvent
>       break;
>     case "last_trade_price":
>       // event: MarketLastTradePriceEvent
>       break;
>     case "tick_size_change":
>       // event: MarketTickSizeChangeEvent
>       break;
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Standard Market Events
> >
> > #### Order Book
> >
> > ```ts MarketBookEvent Type theme={null}
> > type OrderBookLevel = {
> >   price: DecimalString;
> >   size: DecimalString;
> > };
> >
> > type MarketBookEvent = {
> >   topic: "market";
> >   type: "book";
> >   payload: {
> >     conditionId: ConditionId;
> >     assetId: ClobAssetId;
> >     bids: OrderBookLevel[];
> >     asks: OrderBookLevel[];
> >     hash?: string | null;
> >     timestamp?: string | null;
> >     minOrderSize?: DecimalString | null;
> >     tickSize?: DecimalString | null;
> >     negRisk?: boolean | null;
> >     lastTradePrice?: DecimalString | null;
> >   };
> > };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json MarketBookEvent Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "topic": "market",
> >   "type": "book",
> >   "payload": {
> >     "conditionId": "0x747dc809fb79e1b05be09c42d6179459a58de2ef3e40f02484a4e1260f741f75",
> >     "assetId": "107505882767731489358349912513945399560393482969656700824895970500493757150417",
> >     "bids": [{ "price": "0.08", "size": "33343.4" }],
> >     "asks": [{ "price": "0.09", "size": "163939.58" }],
> >     "hash": "0xabc123…",
> >     "timestamp": "1782753357257"
> >   }
> > }
> > ```
> >
> > #### Price Change
> >
> > ```ts MarketPriceChangeEvent Type theme={null}
> > type PriceChange = {
> >   assetId: ClobAssetId;
> >   price: DecimalString;
> >   size: DecimalString;
> >   side: OrderSide;
> >   hash?: string | null;
> >   bestBid?: DecimalString | null;
> >   bestAsk?: DecimalString | null;
> > };
> >
> > type MarketPriceChangeEvent = {
> >   topic: "market";
> >   type: "price_change";
> >   payload: {
> >     conditionId: ConditionId;
> >     priceChanges: PriceChange[];
> >     timestamp?: string | null;
> >   };
> > };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json MarketPriceChangeEvent Example theme={null}

> >       {
> >         "assetId": "107505882767731489358349912513945399560393482969656700824895970500493757150417",
> >         "price": "0.08",
> >         "size": "33343.4",
> >         "side": "BUY",
> >         "hash": "56621a121a47ed9333273e21c83b660cff37ae50",
> >         "bestBid": "0.08",
> >         "bestAsk": "0.09"
> >       }
> >     ],
> >     "timestamp": "1782753357257"
> >   }
> > }
> > ```
> >
> > #### Last Trade Price

> > ```ts MarketLastTradePriceEvent Type theme={null}

> >
> > ```ts MarketTickSizeChangeEvent Type theme={null}
> > type MarketTickSizeChangeEvent = {
> >   topic: "market";
> >   type: "tick_size_change";
> >   payload: {
> >     conditionId: ConditionId;
> >     assetId: ClobAssetId;

> >     newTickSize: DecimalString;

> > ```json MarketTickSizeChangeEvent Example theme={null}

> >     "newTickSize": "0.001",

>
> Enable `customFeatureEnabled` to include top-of-book and market lifecycle
> updates:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const stream = await client.subscribe([
>   {
>     topic: "market",
>     assetIds: [assetId],
>     customFeatureEnabled: true,
>   },
> ]);
>
> for await (const event of stream) {
>   switch (event.type) {
>     case "book":
>       // event: MarketBookEvent
>       break;
>     case "price_change":
>       // event: MarketPriceChangeEvent
>       break;
>     case "last_trade_price":
>       // event: MarketLastTradePriceEvent
>       break;
>     case "tick_size_change":
>       // event: MarketTickSizeChangeEvent
>       break;
>     case "best_bid_ask":
>       // event: MarketBestBidAskEvent
>       break;
>     case "new_market":
>       // event: NewMarketEvent
>       break;
>     case "market_resolved":
>       // event: MarketResolvedEvent
>       break;
>   }
> }
> ```

> [tab] Python
>
> The unified SDK uses `asset_id` for an outcome's trading identifier: a token
> ID for a CTF market or a position ID for a Polymarket Protocol V2 market.
> Use the identifier exposed for that outcome.
>
> Given an `AsyncPublicClient` or `AsyncSecureClient`, subscribe to the market
> stream with a `MarketSpec` containing one or more outcome IDs:
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from polymarket.streams import MarketSpec
>
> asset_id = "<asset_id>"
>
> async with await client.subscribe(
>     MarketSpec(asset_ids=[asset_id]),
> ) as stream:
>     async for event in stream:
>         if event.type == "book":
>             ...  # event: MarketBookEvent
>         elif event.type == "price_change":
>             ...  # event: MarketPriceChangeEvent
>         elif event.type == "last_trade_price":
>             ...  # event: MarketLastTradePriceEvent
>         elif event.type == "tick_size_change":
>             ...  # event: MarketTickSizeChangeEvent
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Standard Market Events
> >
> > #### Order Book
> >
> > ```python MarketBookEvent Type theme={null}
> > class OrderBookLevel:
> >     price: Decimal
> >     size: Decimal
> >
> > class MarketBookPayload:
> >     condition_id: ConditionId
> >     asset_id: ClobAssetId
> >     bids: tuple[OrderBookLevel, ...]
> >     asks: tuple[OrderBookLevel, ...]
> >     hash: str | None
> >     timestamp: datetime | None
> >     min_order_size: Decimal | None
> >     tick_size: Decimal | None
> >     neg_risk: bool | None
> >     last_trade_price: Decimal | None
> >
> > class MarketBookEvent:
> >     topic: Literal["market"]
> >     type: Literal["book"]
> >     payload: MarketBookPayload
> > ```
> >
> > ```json MarketBookEvent Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "topic": "market",
> >   "type": "book",
> >   "payload": {
> >     "condition_id": "0x747dc809fb79e1b05be09c42d6179459a58de2ef3e40f02484a4e1260f741f75",
> >     "asset_id": "107505882767731489358349912513945399560393482969656700824895970500493757150417",
> >     "bids": [{ "price": "0.08", "size": "33343.4" }],
> >     "asks": [{ "price": "0.09", "size": "163939.58" }],
> >     "hash": "0xabc123…",
> >     "timestamp": "2026-06-29T17:15:57.257000Z"
> >   }
> > }
> > ```
> >
> > #### Price Change
> >
> > ```python MarketPriceChangeEvent Type theme={null}
> > class PriceChange:

## Sports Stream

Use the sports stream to keep live game information current alongside sports
markets. Updates arrive when a game goes live, its score or period changes, or
it ends. NFL and CFB updates can also reflect possession changes.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Sports data is provided for informational purposes only. It may be delayed,
> contain errors, or omit recent events. Polymarket does not provide trading or
> investment advice, and this data should not be used as the basis for a trading
> decision.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Given a `PublicClient` or `SecureClient`, subscribe to the `sports` topic to receive
> every game update:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const stream = await client.subscribe([{ topic: "sports" }]);
>
> for await (const event of stream) {
>   // event: SportsEvent
> }
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Sports Event
> >
> > ```ts SportsEvent Type theme={null}
> > type SportsEvent = {
> >   topic: "sports";
> >   type: "sport_result";
> >   payload: {
> >     gameId: number;
> >     sportradarGameId?: string | null;
> >     slug?: string | null;
> >     leagueAbbreviation: string;
> >     homeTeam?: string | null;
> >     awayTeam?: string | null;
> >     status: string;
> >     live: boolean;
> >     ended: boolean;
> >     score: string;
> >     period?: string | null;
> >     elapsed?: string | null;
> >     finishedAt?: IsoDateTimeString | null;
> >     turn?: string | null;
> >   };
> > };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json SportsEvent Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "topic": "sports",
> >   "type": "sport_result",
> >   "payload": {
> >     "gameId": 5127839,
> >     "leagueAbbreviation": "NBA",
> >     "homeTeam": "Los Angeles Lakers",
> >     "awayTeam": "Boston Celtics",
> >     "status": "InProgress",
> >     "live": true,
> >     "ended": false,
> >     "score": "98-94",
> >     "period": "Q4",
> >     "elapsed": "05:12"
> >   }
> > }
> > ```
> >
> > `score` is a combined `"<home>-<away>"` string, not separate home and away
> > fields.

> [tab] Python
>
> Given an `AsyncPublicClient` or `AsyncSecureClient`, subscribe with a
> `SportsSpec` to receive every game update:
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from polymarket.streams import SportsSpec
>
> async with await client.subscribe(SportsSpec()) as stream:
>     async for event in stream:
>         ...  # event: SportsEvent
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Sports Event
> >
> > ```python SportsEvent Type theme={null}
> > class SportsGameResult:
> >     game_id: int
> >     sportradar_game_id: str | None
> >     slug: str | None
> >     league_abbreviation: str
> >     home_team: str | None
> >     away_team: str | None
> >     status: str
> >     live: bool
> >     ended: bool
> >     score: str
> >     period: str | None
> >     elapsed: str | None
> >     finished_at: datetime | None
> >     turn: str | None
> >
> > class SportsResultEvent:
> >     topic: Literal["sports"]
> >     type: Literal["sport_result"]
> >     payload: SportsGameResult
> >
> > SportsEvent = SportsResultEvent
> > ```
> >
> > ```json SportsEvent Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "topic": "sports",
> >   "type": "sport_result",
> >   "payload": {
> >     "game_id": 5127839,
> >     "league_abbreviation": "NBA",
> >     "home_team": "Los Angeles Lakers",
> >     "away_team": "Boston Celtics",
> >     "status": "InProgress",
> >     "live": true,
> >     "ended": false,
> >     "score": "98-94",
> >     "period": "Q4",
> >     "elapsed": "05:12"
> >   }
> > }
> > ```
> >
> > `score` is a combined `"<home>-<away>"` string, not separate home and away
> > fields.

> [tab] API
>
> Connect to the sports WebSocket:
>
> ```text theme={null}
> wss://sports-api.polymarket.com/ws
> ```
>
> > [!NOTE]
> >
> > The sports WebSocket uses an application-level heartbeat. The server sends the
> > text frame `ping` every 5 seconds; reply with `pong` within 10 seconds or the
> > server closes the connection.
>
> Once connected, the server starts streaming every game update. No
> subscription frame is required.
>
> > [accordion] Sports Event
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > {
> >   "gameId": 5127839,
> >   "leagueAbbreviation": "NBA",
> >   "homeTeam": "Los Angeles Lakers",
> >   "awayTeam": "Boston Celtics",
> >   "status": "InProgress",
> >   "live": true,
> >   "ended": false,
> >   "score": "98-94",
> >   "period": "Q4",
> >   "elapsed": "05:12"
> > }
> > ```
> >
> > Sports messages have no envelope or event-type field. Each message is the
> > game update object itself, and `score` is a combined `"<home>-<away>"`
> > string.

### Period Values

The meaning and format of a period depend on the sport:

| Values | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `1H`, `2H` | First or second half |
| `1Q`, `2Q`, `3Q`, `4Q` | Quarter |
| `HT` | Halftime |
| `FT` | Full time in regulation |
| `FT OT` | Full time after overtime |
| `FT NR` | Full time with no result |
| `End 1`, `End 2`, … | End of an MLB inning |
| `1/3`, `2/3`, `3/3` | Map number in a best-of-three series |
| `1/5`, `2/5`, … | Map number in a best-of-five series |

### Game Status Values

Status values vary by sport and are case-sensitive:

| Sport | Values |
| - | - |
| NFL | `Scheduled`, `InProgress`, `Final`, `F/OT`, `Suspended`, `Postponed`, `Delayed`, `Canceled`, `Forfeit`, `NotNecessary` |
| NHL | `Scheduled`, `InProgress`, `Final`, `F/OT`, `F/SO`, `Suspended`, `Postponed`, `Delayed`, `Canceled`, `Forfeit`, `NotNecessary` |
| MLB | `Scheduled`, `InProgress`, `Final`, `Suspended`, `Delayed`, `Postponed`, `Canceled`, `Forfeit`, `NotNecessary` |
| NBA and CBB | `Scheduled`, `InProgress`, `Final`, `F/OT`, `Suspended`, `Postponed`, `Delayed`, `Canceled`, `Forfeit`, `NotNecessary` |
| CFB | `Scheduled`, `InProgress`, `Final`, `F/OT`, `Suspended`, `Postponed`, `Delayed`, `Canceled`, `Forfeit` |
| Soccer | `Scheduled`, `InProgress`, `Break`, `Suspended`, `PenaltyShootout`, `Final`, `Awarded`, `Postponed`, `Canceled` |
| Esports | `not_started`, `running`, `finished`, `postponed`, `canceled` |
| Tennis | `scheduled`, `inprogress`, `suspended`, `finished`, `postponed`, `cancelled` |

## Reference Prices

Stream crypto, equity, and time-weighted average reference prices through Polymarket. Authenticate, select the symbols you need, and process historical prices and live updates.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Reference price subscriptions require authentication.
> Existing RTDS integrations should follow the [migration
> guide](/migrate/rtds-to-polybolt).

Use lowercase symbols. See the [PolyBolt overview](/api-reference/live-data/overview#supported-symbols) for crypto and TWAP lists, and the equity catalog below for equity symbols.

### Historical Snapshot

Each new subscription provides a snapshot of the preceding two minutes of prices and live updates. Seed local state from the snapshot, then apply the latest price. Applications that only need live prices can ignore the snapshot.

### Crypto Prices

Stream crypto reference prices in USD to keep prices current alongside related markets.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Call `client.subscribe` with an authenticated `SecureClient` from `@polymarket/client` 0.11.0 or later. See [Wallet Integrations](/getting-started/typescript#wallet-integrations) to create the client.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const stream = await client.subscribe([
>   { topic: "prices.crypto", symbols: ["btcusd", "ethusd"] },
> ]);
>
> try {
>   for await (const event of stream) {
>     // event: CryptoPriceEvent
>     if (event.type === "subscribe") {
>       const history = event.payload.data;
>       // Seed local state from the snapshot.
>     } else {
>       const price = event.payload.value;
>       const observedAt = event.payload.timestamp;
>       // Apply the latest price.
>     }
>   }
> } finally {
>   await stream.close();
> }
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: CryptoPriceEvent
> >

> >

> >         symbol: string;
> >         data: { timestamp: EpochMilliseconds; value: DecimalString }[];
> >       };
> >     }
> >   | {
> >       topic: "prices.crypto";
> >       type: "update";
> >       timestamp: EpochMilliseconds;
> >       seq?: number;

> >       payload: {
> >         symbol: string;
> >         timestamp: EpochMilliseconds;

> [tab] API
>
> Connect to PolyBolt and authenticate before subscribing to crypto prices.
>
> **1. Connect**
>
> Open a WebSocket connection to:
>
> ```text theme={null}
> wss://ws-live-v2.polymarket.com/ws
> ```
>
> **2. Authenticate**
>
> Send your [CLOB API credentials](/getting-started/api#authentication) on the open connection:
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "op": "auth",
>   "rid": "a1",
>   "auth": {
>     "apiKey": "<api key>",
>     "secret": "<api secret>",
>     "passphrase": "<api passphrase>"
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> **3. Wait for Authentication**
>
> Wait for the server to confirm authentication before sending a subscription:
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "op": "authed",
>   "rid": "a1"
> }
> ```
>
> **4. Subscribe to Crypto Prices**
>
> Send this frame on the authenticated connection to subscribe to BTC/USD:
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "op": "subscribe",
>   "rid": "s1",
>   "subscriptions": [
>     {
>       "channel": "price.crypto",
>       "filter": {
>         "symbol": "btcusd"
>       }
>     }
>   ]
> }
> ```

#### Supported Equity Symbols

| Asset class | Supported symbols |
| - | - |
| Stocks | `aapl`, `tsla`, `msft`, `googl`, `amzn`, `meta`, `nvda`, `nflx`, `pltr`, `open`, `rklb`, `abnb`, `coin`, `hood` |
| ETFs | `qqq`, `spy`, `ewy`, `vxx` |
| Forex | `eurusd`, `gbpusd`, `usdcad`, `usdjpy`, `usdkrw`, `usdchf`, `usdmxn`, `usdzar`, `usdbrl`, `usdnok`, `usdsek`, `usdtry` |
| Precious metals | `xauusd`, `xagusd` |
| Commodities | `wti`, `cc`, `ngd` |

#### Read the Market Status

Use market status to distinguish a closed market from a price that has stopped
updating. Status describes the instrument priced by the provider, so two
providers can report different states for the same symbol. For example, a
Chainlink series can remain open over a weekend while a Pyth series follows the
underlying exchange's session hours.

| Status | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `open` | The provider reports that its instrument's market is trading. |
| `closed` | The provider reports that its instrument's market is closed. |
| `unknown` | The provider cannot determine the market's state. |
| Not stated | No status was supplied. Do not assume the market is open. |

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> In SDK 0.14.0 and later, read `payload.marketStatus` on both `subscribe` snapshots
> and `update` events. Import `EquityMarketStatus` from `@polymarket/client` and use
> an existing authenticated `SecureClient`:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { EquityMarketStatus } from "@polymarket/client";
>
> const stream = await client.subscribe([
>   { topic: "prices.equity", symbol: "aapl" },
> ]);
>
> try {
>   for await (const event of stream) {
>     const status = event.payload.marketStatus;
>     if (status === EquityMarketStatus.Closed) {
>       console.log(event.payload.symbol, "Market closed");
>     } else if (status === EquityMarketStatus.Unknown || status === undefined) {
>       console.log(event.payload.symbol, "Market state unavailable");
>     }
>   }
> } finally {
>   await stream.close();
> }
> ```
>
> `EquityMarketStatus.Open`, `.Closed`, and `.Unknown` correspond to the three stated
> values. `undefined` means not stated. The same field is available on
> `prices.equity.twap`. Subscribe with `{ topic: "prices.equity.twap", symbol: "eurusd" }`.
> In a snapshot, status is on `payload`, alongside `data`, rather than on each
> historical price point.

> [tab] Python
>
> In SDK 0.14.0 and later, read `payload.market_status` on both `subscribe` snapshots
> and `update` events. Import `EquityMarketStatus` from `polymarket.streams` and use
> an existing authenticated `AsyncSecureClient`:
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from polymarket.streams import EquityMarketStatus, EquityPriceSpec
>
> async with await client.subscribe(EquityPriceSpec(symbol="aapl")) as stream:
>     async for event in stream:
>         status = event.payload.market_status
>         if status == EquityMarketStatus.CLOSED:
>             print(event.payload.symbol, "Market closed")
>         elif status is None or status == EquityMarketStatus.UNKNOWN:
>             print(event.payload.symbol, "Market state unavailable")
> ```
>
> `EquityMarketStatus.OPEN`, `.CLOSED`, and `.UNKNOWN` correspond to the three stated
> values. `None` means not stated. For equity TWAP, import `EquityTwapPriceSpec` from
> `polymarket.streams` and pass `EquityTwapPriceSpec(symbol="eurusd")`. Its payload
> has the same `market_status` field. In a snapshot, read status from `payload`,
> rather than from the historical points in `payload.data`.

> [tab] API
>
> Read `payload.market_status` on `price.equity` and `price.equity.twap`. A missing
> field means not stated. On an authenticated PolyBolt WebSocket connection,
> send this subscription frame:
>
> ```json Subscribe theme={null}
> {
>   "op": "subscribe",
>   "rid": "s2",
>   "subscriptions": [
>     {
>       "channel": "price.equity",
>       "filter": { "symbol": "aapl", "provider": "pyth" }
>     }
>   ]
> }
> ```
>
> These examples show a received status-only spot update and a snapshot with
> status at batch level:
>
> ```json Status-Only Update theme={null}
> {
>   "v": 1,
>   "channel": "price.equity",
>   "seq": 41,
>   "ts": 1792526399800,
>   "payload": {
>     "symbol": "aapl",
>     "value": 262.71,
>     "full_accuracy_value": "262.71",
>     "timestamp": 1792526399800,
>     "received_at": 1792526401200,
>     "is_carried_forward": true,
>     "source": "pyth",
>     "market_status": "closed"
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> ```json Snapshot theme={null}
> {
>   "v": 1,
>   "channel": "price.equity",
>   "seq": 1,
>   "ts": 1792526399800,
>   "snapshot": true,
>   "payload": {
>     "symbol": "aapl",
>     "source": "pyth",
>     "market_status": "closed",
>     "data": [
>       {
>         "timestamp": 1792526399800,
>         "value": 262.71,
>         "full_accuracy_value": "262.71"
>       }
>     ]
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> See the [PolyBolt overview](/api-reference/live-data/overview#read-the-market-status)
> for the wire contract and provider behavior.

A spot status change can repeat the last price and its timestamp. The update is
marked as carried forward (`isCarriedForward` in TypeScript,
`is_carried_forward` in Python and the API). **Do not discard an update solely
because its price timestamp repeats**: doing so can hide a market close or reopen.
Equity TWAP status changes arrive with a new price.

While status is closed or unknown, a snapshot can retain a closing price older
than the usual two-minute history window. Re-read status and source after every
reconnect. SDK cached spot snapshots retain the last stated status when a later
update omits it. A status change on an older price does not roll newer history
back. An unstated live update still has `undefined` or `None` for its own status.

During market hours, prices can update up to five times per second for each feed.

### TWAP Prices

A time-weighted average price (TWAP) represents an asset's price across a lookback window. Stream Chainlink-computed crypto TWAPs with a fixed 60-second window through Polymarket.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Call `client.subscribe` to subscribe to the `prices.crypto.twap` topic and your chosen symbols with an authenticated `SecureClient`.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const stream = await client.subscribe([
>   { topic: "prices.crypto.twap", symbols: ["btcusd"] },
> ]);
>
> try {
>   for await (const event of stream) {
>     // event: CryptoTwapPriceEvent
>     if (event.type === "subscribe") {
>       const history = event.payload.data;
>       // Seed local state from the snapshot.
>     } else {
>       const price = event.payload.value;
>       const observedAt = event.payload.timestamp;
>       // Apply the latest price.
>     }
>   }
> } finally {
>   await stream.close();
> }
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: CryptoTwapPriceEvent
> >
> > **events: CryptoTwapPriceEvent\[]**
> >
> > ```ts CryptoTwapPriceEvent Union theme={null}
> > type CryptoTwapPriceEvent =
> >   | {
> >       topic: "prices.crypto.twap";
> >       type: "subscribe";
> >       timestamp: EpochMilliseconds;
> >       seq?: number;
> >       dropped?: number;
> >       payload: {
> >         symbol: string;
> >         data: { timestamp: EpochMilliseconds; value: DecimalString }[];
> >         windowSeconds: 60;
> >       };
> >     }
> >   | {
> >       topic: "prices.crypto.twap";
> >       type: "update";
> >       timestamp: EpochMilliseconds;
> >       seq?: number;
> >       dropped?: number;
> >       payload: {
> >         symbol: string;
> >         timestamp: EpochMilliseconds;
> >         value: DecimalString;
> >         windowSeconds: 60;
> >       };
> >     };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json CryptoTwapPriceEvent Example theme={null}
> > [
> >   {
> >     "topic": "prices.crypto.twap",
> >     "type": "subscribe",
> >     "timestamp": 1788886175000,
> >     "seq": 2,
> >     "payload": {
> >       "symbol": "btcusd",
> >       "data": [
> >         {
> >           "timestamp": 1788886057000,
> >           "value": "78788.525642908795142144"
> >         },
> >         {
> >           "timestamp": 1788886058000,
> >           "value": "78788.786579938813673472"
> >         },
> >         {
> >           "timestamp": 1788886059000,
> >           "value": "78789.052518750893375488"
> >         }
> >       ],
> >       "windowSeconds": 60
> >     }
> >   },
> >   {
> >     "topic": "prices.crypto.twap",
> >     "type": "update",
> >     "timestamp": 1788886177000,
> >     "seq": 3,
> >     "payload": {
> >       "symbol": "btcusd",
> >       "timestamp": 1788886177000,
> >       "value": "78803.715261094101516288",
> >       "windowSeconds": 60
> >     }
> >   }
> > ]
> > ```
>
> For live prices only, skip events whose `type` is `"subscribe"`. `payload.value` is already an exact decimal string. No E18 conversion is needed.
>
> Use a canonical symbol such as `btcusd`. The returned `windowSeconds: 60` describes the lookback period, not the update interval. Use `payload.timestamp` to check price freshness.

> > class RealtimeTwapUpdate:
> >     symbol: str
> >     timestamp: datetime
> >     value: Decimal
> >     window_seconds: Literal[60]
> >
> > class CryptoTwapPriceSnapshotEvent:
> >     topic: Literal["prices.crypto.twap"]
> >     type: Literal["subscribe"]
> >     timestamp: datetime
> >     seq: int | None
> >     dropped: int | None
> >     payload: RealtimeTwapSnapshot
> >
> > class CryptoTwapPriceUpdateEvent:
> >     topic: Literal["prices.crypto.twap"]
> >     type: Literal["update"]
> >     timestamp: datetime
> >     seq: int | None
> >     dropped: int | None
> >     payload: RealtimeTwapUpdate
> >
> > CryptoTwapPriceEvent = CryptoTwapPriceSnapshotEvent | CryptoTwapPriceUpdateEvent
> > ```
> >
> > ```json CryptoTwapPriceEvent Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "timestamp": "2026-09-08T16:49:37Z",
> >   "seq": 3,
> >   "topic": "prices.crypto.twap",
> >   "type": "update",
> >   "payload": {
> >     "timestamp": "2026-09-08T16:49:37Z",
> >     "value": "78803.715261094101516288",
> >     "symbol": "btcusd",
> >     "window_seconds": 60
> >   }
> > }
> > ```
>
> Values are `Decimal`, and timestamps are UTC `datetime` objects.
>
> `payload.window_seconds` is always `60` and describes the lookback window. Use `payload.value` directly without E18 scaling, and use `payload.timestamp` to check freshness.

> [tab] API
>
> Reuse the authenticated connection from the [Crypto Prices](#crypto-prices) API example and send this frame to subscribe to the 60-second BTC/USD TWAP:
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "op": "subscribe",
>   "rid": "s3",
>   "subscriptions": [
>     {
>       "channel": "price.crypto.twap",
>       "filter": {
>         "symbol": "btcusd",
>         "window_seconds": 60
>       }
>     }
>   ]
> }
> ```

## Comments

> [!WARNING]
>
> Live comment and reaction streaming is being retired without a replacement
> streaming channel. Check below for the corresponding fetch method.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Create a public client and call `client.listComments()` to list comments for an event. This method does not provide live comment or reaction events.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import {
>   CommentParentEntityType,
>   createPublicClient,
> } from "@polymarket/client";
>
> const client = createPublicClient();
> const pages = client.listComments({
>   parentEntityId: "18396",
>   parentEntityType: CommentParentEntityType.Event,
>   pageSize: 20,
>   order: "id",
>   ascending: true,
> });
> const page = await pages.firstPage();
>
> console.log(page.items);
> ```
>
> `page.items` contains `Comment` objects. Check `page.hasMore` for more results and continue with `pages.from(page.nextCursor)`.
>
> > [accordion] Output: Comment
> >
> > One comment from `page.items`, serialized as JSON with selected fields shown.
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > {
> >   "id": "1020073",
> >   "body": "@truce @yayyo",
> >   "parentEntityType": "Event",
> >   "parentEntityID": "18396",
> >   "createdAt": "2025-02-12T00:48:05.40822Z",
> >   "reactionCount": 2
> > }
> > ```

> [tab] Python
>
> Create a public client and call `client.list_comments()` to list comments for an event. This method does not provide live comment or reaction events.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from polymarket import AsyncPublicClient
>
> async with AsyncPublicClient() as client:
>     pages = client.list_comments(
>         parent_entity_id="18396",
>         parent_entity_type="Event",
>         page_size=20,
>         order="id",
>         ascending=True,
>     )
>     page = await pages.first_page()
>
>     print(page.items)
> ```
>
> `page.items` contains `Comment` objects. Check `page.has_more` for more results and continue with `pages.from_cursor(page.next_cursor)`.
>
> > [accordion] Output: Comment
> >
> > One comment from `page.items`, serialized as JSON with selected fields shown.
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > {
> >   "id": "1020073",
> >   "body": "@truce @yayyo",
> >   "parent_entity_type": "Event",
> >   "parent_entity_id": "18396",
> >   "created_at": "2025-02-12T00:48:05.408220Z",
> >   "reaction_count": 2
> > }
> > ```

> [tab] API
>
> Use `GET /comments` on the Gamma API to list comments for an event. This request does not provide live comment or reaction events.
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl --get "https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/comments" \
>   --data-urlencode "parent_entity_id=18396" \
>   --data-urlencode "parent_entity_type=Event" \
>   --data-urlencode "limit=20" \
>   --data-urlencode "offset=0" \
>   --data-urlencode "order=id" \
>   --data-urlencode "ascending=true"
> ```
>
> The response is an array of comments.
>
> > [accordion] Output: Comment\[]
> >
> > First comment in the response, with selected fields shown.
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > [
> >   {
> >     "id": "1020073",
> >     "body": "@truce @yayyo",
> >     "parentEntityType": "Event",
> >     "parentEntityID": 18396,
