### Fills

Use fills to reconcile executions, fees, realized PnL, and exposure changes.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const pages = session.listFills({
>   instrumentId: 1,
>   start: Date.now() - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
>   end: Date.now(),
> });
>
> for await (const page of pages) {
>   // page.items: PerpsAccountFill[]
> }
> ```
>
> Each page returns execution records you can use to reconcile fees, PnL, and exposure.
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsAccountFill\[]
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > [
> >   {
> >     "tradeId": 987654321,
> >     "orderId": 1234567890,
> >     "instrumentId": 1,
> >     "side": "long",
> >     "price": "65000",
> >     "quantity": "0.01",
> >     "taker": true,
> >     "fee": "0.26",
> >     "feeAsset": "pUSD",
> >     "previousSize": "0",
> >     "previousEntryPrice": "0",
> >     "pnl": "0",
> >     "liquidation": false,
> >     "adl": false,
> >     "settlement": false,
> >     "timestamp": 1767000010500,
> >     "hash": "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111"
> >   }
> > ]
> > ```
>
> `instrumentId` accepts an integer from `0` through `4294967295`. Omit it to read all
> instruments. Keep the same filter while paging. `adl` identifies an
> auto-deleveraging fill and is separate from the liquidation flag.
>
> For a backstop liquidation, the optional details object has this shape:
>
> ```json PerpsLiquidationDetails Example theme={null}
> {
>   "mark": "65000.00",
>   "method": "backstop"
> }
> ```
>
> When present, `liquidationDetails` contains `mark`, `method`, and an optional
> `liquidatedUser` address. `mark` is the decimal string mark price captured when the
> liquidation was issued. The fill's `price` remains its accounting execution
> price. `method` is `"backstop"` or `"market"`. Only backstop fills currently
> include these details. The same data is available in private fill updates.
>
> `settlement: true` identifies a position close at the final instrument-settlement
> price. The same flag is available on each fill in a session `"fill"` event
> payload; it defaults to `false` on older responses.

> [tab] Python
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
>
> end = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
> start = end - timedelta(days=1)
>
> pages = session.list_fills(instrument_id=1, start=start, end=end)
>
> async for page in pages:
>     # page.items: tuple[PerpsFill, ...]
>     pass
> ```
>
> Each page returns execution records you can use to reconcile fees, PnL, and exposure.
>
> > [accordion] Output: tuple\[PerpsFill, ...]
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > [
> >   {
> >     "trade_id": 987654321,
> >     "order_id": 1234567890,
> >     "instrument_id": 1,
> >     "side": "long",
> >     "price": "65000",
> >     "quantity": "0.01",
> >     "taker": true,
> >     "fee": "0.26",
> >     "fee_asset": "pUSD",
> >     "previous_size": "0",
> >     "previous_entry_price": "0",
> >     "pnl": "0",
> >     "liquidation": false,
> >     "adl": false,
> >     "settlement": false,
> >     "timestamp": "2025-12-29T09:20:10.500000Z",
> >     "hash": "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111"
> >   }
> > ]
> > ```
>
> `instrument_id` accepts an integer from `0` through `4294967295`. Omit it to read all
> instruments. Keep the same filter while paging. `adl` identifies an
> auto-deleveraging fill and is separate from the liquidation flag.
>
> For a backstop liquidation, the optional details object has this shape:
>
> ```json PerpsLiquidationDetails Example theme={null}
> {
>   "mark": "65000.00",
>   "method": "backstop"
> }
> ```
>
> When present, `liquidation_details` contains `mark`, `method`, and an optional
> `liquidated_user` address. `mark` is the `Decimal` mark price captured when the
> liquidation was issued. The fill's `price` remains its accounting execution
> price. `method` is `"backstop"` or `"market"`. Only backstop fills currently
> include these details. The same data is available in private fill updates.
>
> `settlement=True` identifies a position close at the final instrument-settlement
> price. The same flag is available on each `PerpsFill` in a session `"fill"` event
> payload; it defaults to `False` on older responses. Fill timestamps are UTC
> `datetime` values; the JSON above shows their serialization.

> [tab] API
>
> ```bash theme={null}

>   -H "polymarket-proxy: <proxy_address>" \
>   -H "polymarket-secret: <proxy_secret>" \

>   --data-urlencode "end_timestamp=1767000000000" \
>   --data-urlencode "instrument_id=1"
> ```
>
> Use the response's `more` field to continue fetching older or newer records.
> Pass `instrument_id` to narrow the pages to one instrument's fills.
>
> Each page returns execution records you can use to reconcile fees, PnL, and exposure.
>
> > [accordion] Output: Fills
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > {
> >   "data": [
> >     {
> >       "trade_id": 987654321,
> >       "order_id": 1234567890,
> >       "instrument_id": 1,
> >       "side": "long",
> >       "price": "65000",
> >       "quantity": "0.01",
> >       "taker": true,
> >       "fee": "0.26",
> >       "fee_asset": "pUSD",
> >       "previous_size": "0",
> >       "previous_entry_price": "0",
> >       "pnl": "0",
> >       "liquidation": false,
> >       "settlement": false,
> >       "adl": false,
> >       "timestamp": 1767000010500,
> >       "hash": "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111"
> >     }
> >   ],
> >   "more": false
> > }
> > ```
>
> `instrument_id` accepts an integer from `0` through `4294967295`. Omit it to read all
> instruments. Keep the same filter while paging. `adl` identifies an
> auto-deleveraging fill and is separate from the liquidation flag.
>
> For a backstop liquidation, the optional details object has this shape:
>
> ```json LiquidationDetails Example theme={null}
> {
>   "mark": "65000.00",
>   "method": "backstop"
> }
> ```
>
> When present, `liquidation_details` contains `mark`, `method`, and an optional
> `liquidated_user` address. `mark` is the decimal string mark price captured when the
> liquidation was issued. The fill's `price` remains its accounting execution
> price. `method` is `"backstop"` or `"market"`. Only backstop fills currently
> include these details. The same data is available in private fill updates.
>
> `settlement: true` identifies a position close at the final instrument-settlement
> price. The same flag appears on each entry in `data` on the private `fills`
> WebSocket channel.

Settlement fills carry no fees or liquidation penalties. Reconcile them as
position closures, separately from ordinary market executions and ADL.

## Inspect Position Snapshots

Inspect a position now or immediately after a selected fill. Each snapshot covers
one position cycle, from opening until the position becomes flat or changes side.
Select up to 20 active instruments and 4 historical fills in one request, with at
least one selection. Results keep the selection order within each group.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Use the existing authenticated `session` to read your own positions. The example
> selects instrument `1`; replace it with the instrument you want to inspect.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { PerpsPositionSnapshotStatus } from "@polymarket/client";
>
> const snapshots = await session.fetchPositionSnapshots({
>   activeInstrumentIds: [1],
> });
>
> for (const item of snapshots.active) {
>   if (item.status === PerpsPositionSnapshotStatus.Ok) {
>     console.log(item.snapshot.pnl, item.snapshot.leverage);
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsPositionSnapshots
> >
> > A successful active selection returns:
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > {
> >   "historyAsOfAt": 1767000010500,
> >   "active": [
> >     {
> >       "instrumentId": 1,
> >       "status": "ok",
> >       "snapshot": {
> >         "positionCycleId": "opaque:cycle",
> >         "side": "long",
> >         "startedAt": 1767000000000,
> >         "asOfAt": 1767000010500,
> >         "isClosed": false,
> >         "sizeAfter": "1",
> >         "entryPrice": "100",
> >         "asOfPrice": "110",
> >         "pnl": "10",
> >         "pnlPercent": "50",
> >         "leverage": 5,
> >         "chart": {
> >           "candles": [
> >             {
> >               "position": 0,
> >               "open": 100,
> >               "high": 110,
> >               "low": 100,
> >               "close": 110
> >             }
> >           ],
> >           "markers": [
> >             {
> >               "position": 0,
> >               "kind": "increase"
> >             }
> >           ]
> >         }
> >       }
> >     }
> >   ],
> >   "history": []
> > }
> > ```
> >
> > For `Ok`, `snapshot` is a `PerpsPositionSnapshot`. Financial values such as `pnl`
> > use `DecimalString`; timestamps are Unix milliseconds. `pnlPercent` and `leverage`
> > can be `null`.
>
> To inspect the fill shown in the Fills example, add `historyFills`. Keep the
> original decimal trade ID as a string; do not round it through a JavaScript number.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import type { PerpsPositionSnapshotFill } from "@polymarket/client";
>
> const fill: PerpsPositionSnapshotFill = {
>   instrumentId: 1,
>   tradeId: "987654321",
>   timestamp: 1767000010500,
> };
> const historical = await session.fetchPositionSnapshots({
>   historyFills: [fill],
> });
> // historical.history preserves selection order and includes canonical string tradeId.
> ```
>
> For a public read, call `client.fetchPerpsPositionSnapshots({ address,
>     activeInstrumentIds: [1] })` with a `createPublicClient()` instance and the
> registered account's address. This method does not add session credentials,
> including when inherited by a secure client.

> [tab] Python
>
> Use the existing authenticated `session` to read your own positions. The example
> selects instrument `1`; replace it with the instrument you want to inspect.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> snapshots = await session.fetch_position_snapshots(active_instrument_ids=(1,))
>
> for item in snapshots.active:
>     if item.status == "ok":
>         print(item.snapshot.pnl, item.snapshot.leverage)
> ```

> >         "is_closed": false,

> >         "as_of_price": "110",

> >

> > as `pnl` are `Decimal`; timestamps, including `history_as_of_at`, are UTC
> > `datetime` values. `pnl_percent` and `leverage` can be `None`.
>
> To inspect the fill shown in the Fills example, select its instrument, decimal
> trade ID, and original timestamp. `timestamp` accepts an aware `datetime` with
> whole milliseconds or an integer Unix millisecond timestamp.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from polymarket import PerpsPositionSnapshotFill
>
> fill = PerpsPositionSnapshotFill(
>     instrument_id=1,
>     trade_id="987654321",
>     timestamp=1767000010500,
> )
> historical = await session.fetch_position_snapshots(history_fills=(fill,))
> # historical.history preserves selection order and includes canonical string trade_id.
> ```
>
> For a public read, use
> `await client.fetch_perps_position_snapshots(address=address, active_instrument_ids=(1,))`
> with an `AsyncPublicClient` and the registered account's address. This method does
> not add session credentials, including when inherited by an async secure client.

> [tab] API
>
> Send a `POST` to `/v1/info/position-snapshots`. Supply your registered account
> address and owner credentials for private leverage and PnL percentage.
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/info/position-snapshots" \
>   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -H "polymarket-proxy: <proxy_address>" \
>   -H "polymarket-secret: <proxy_secret>" \

> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: Position Snapshots
> >

> >

> >     {
> >       "instrument_id": 1,
> >       "status": "ok",
> >       "snapshot": {
> >         "position_cycle_id": "opaque:cycle",
> >         "side": "long",
> >         "started_at": 1767000000000,
> >         "as_of_at": 1767000010500,
> >         "is_closed": false,
> >         "size_after": "1",
> >         "entry_price": "100",
> >         "as_of_price": "110",
> >         "pnl": "10",
> >         "pnl_percent": "50",
> >         "leverage": 5,
> >         "chart": {
> >           "candles": [
> >             {
> >               "position": 0,
> >               "open": 100,
> >               "high": 110,

> >             }

> >             }

> >       }
> >     }
> >   ],
> >   "history": []
> > }
> > ```
> >
> > Only `status: "ok"` includes `snapshot`. Financial values such as `pnl` are decimal
> > strings; timestamps are Unix milliseconds. `pnl_percent` and `leverage` can be `null`.
>
> For historical selections, add `history_fills` containing `instrument_id`,
> `trade_id` as a decimal string, and `timestamp` in Unix milliseconds. IDs can span
> the full UInt64 range; returned IDs omit leading zeroes. Duplicate instruments or
> fill identities and explicit `null` arrays return HTTP 400. Unknown accounts also
> return HTTP 400. Each fill timestamp must be at most `18446744073709`.
>
> Omit both credential headers for a public read. Invalid supplied credentials
> return HTTP 401; credentials for another account do not reveal the selected
> account's private values. HTTP 503 indicates admission or shared dependency
> failure; retry with backoff.

### Interpret a Snapshot

While a cycle remains open, PnL is gross unrealized profit or loss on its remaining
size. After it closes, PnL is the gross realized total for that cycle. Both exclude
fees, funding, and previous cycles. A fill that closes or flips a position returns
the closed cycle; the new cycle appears in the active selection or its later fills.

Leverage and PnL percentage are visible only to the authenticated owner. Historical
leverage uses the value captured at the selected fill and can remain unavailable.
PnL percentage uses nominal entry margin, so it can differ from portfolio return
on equity. Chart candles and markers use numeric coordinates and approximate
prices; the selected minute's candle includes the whole minute's aggregate.

### Handle Unavailable Selections

Only successful selections contain a snapshot. The completed-history horizon
indicates how far the serving gateway has processed history; gateways can report
different horizons. Handle each selection independently instead of discarding the
whole batch when one selection is unavailable.

| Status | Next Action |
| - | - |
| `ok` | Use the snapshot. |
| `not_found` | No current position or owned fill was found within the reported horizon; check the selection and horizon. |
| `history_pending` | Retry with backoff while history catches up or historical reconstruction becomes available. |
| `history_limit` | The available reconstruction window does not include the cycle's opening fill. |
| `resource_limit` | Reconstruction exceeded a row, memory, or chart bound. |
| `temporarily_unavailable` | Retry with backoff after a deadline, pricing, or dependency failure. |
| `unavailable` | The cycle cannot be reconstructed safely, for example after a self-match or an unsupported position adjustment. |

Reconstruction limits and unsafe-accounting results are not signals to poll
indefinitely.

## Reconcile Funding and Transfers

Funding, deposits, and withdrawals explain collateral changes that did not come
from order fills. Use [Fund Your Account](/perps/fund-your-account) for deposit
and withdrawal submission workflows.

### Funding Payments

> [tab] TypeScript

> }

### Withdrawals

Use withdrawals to reconcile collateral leaving the Perps account.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const withdrawals = session.listWithdrawals();
>
> for await (const page of withdrawals) {
>   // page.items: PerpsWithdrawal[]
> }
> ```
>
> Each page returns withdrawals you can match against collateral leaving the account.
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsWithdrawal\[]
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > [
> >   {
> >     "withdrawalId": 1234567891,
> >     "asset": "pUSD",
> >     "amount": "50",
> >     "fee": "1.5",
> >     "status": "confirmed",
> >     "to": "0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678",
> >     "hash": "0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333",
> >     "confirmations": 12,
> >     "requiredConfirmations": 12,
> >     "createdTimestamp": 1767000010000,
> >     "confirmedTimestamp": 1767000030000
> >   }
> > ]
> > ```
>
> Branch on `status` using the `PerpsKnownWithdrawalStatus` enum.
>
> | `status` | Meaning |
> | - | - |
> | `PerpsKnownWithdrawalStatus.Pending` | The withdrawal was accepted and is awaiting on-chain confirmation. |
> | `PerpsKnownWithdrawalStatus.Confirmed` | The on-chain transaction reached the required confirmations and the funds were sent to the destination. |
> | `PerpsKnownWithdrawalStatus.Removed` | A chain reorganization removed the on-chain transaction after it was observed. |
> | `PerpsKnownWithdrawalStatus.Failed` | The withdrawal could not be executed on-chain and was reverted; the amount was credited back to the account. |
>
> The status set can grow between SDK releases. `status` is typed
> `PerpsWithdrawalStatus`, so a status added after your release arrives as a
> plain string instead of failing the response parse.

>

## Track Equity and PnL

Use equity and PnL history to explain how the account's value changed over time.

### Equity

Use equity history to chart account value over time. Each point is the last
equity sample in its `interval` bucket, stamped with that sample's own
timestamp. A coarser interval lets each 1000-point page cover a longer window
before `more` is set.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const equity = session.listEquityHistory({
>   interval: "1h",
>   start: Date.now() - 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
>   end: Date.now(),
> });
>
> for await (const page of equity) {
>   // page.items: PerpsEquityPoint[]
> }
> ```
>
> Each page returns points you can plot as account equity over time.
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsEquityPoint\[]
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > [
> >   {
> >     "timestamp": 1767000000000,
> >     "equity": "1000"
> >   }
> > ]
> > ```

> [tab] Python
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
>
> end = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
> start = end - timedelta(days=7)
>
> equity = session.list_equity_history(
>     interval="1h",
>     start=start,
>     end=end,
> )
>
> async for page in equity:
>     # page.items: tuple[PerpsEquityPoint, ...]
>     pass
> ```
>
> Each page returns points you can plot as account equity over time.
>
> > [accordion] Output: tuple\[PerpsEquityPoint, ...]
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > [
> >   {
> >     "timestamp": 1767000000000,
> >     "equity": "1000"
> >   }
> > ]
> > ```

> [tab] API
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl -G "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/account/equity" \
>   -H "polymarket-proxy: <proxy_address>" \
>   -H "polymarket-secret: <proxy_secret>" \
>   --data-urlencode "interval=1h" \
>   --data-urlencode "start_timestamp=1766395200000" \
>   --data-urlencode "end_timestamp=1767000000000"
> ```
>
> Use the response's `more` field to continue fetching older or newer records.
>
> Each page returns points you can plot as account equity over time.
>
> > [accordion] Output: Equity
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > {
> >   "data": [[1767000000000, "1000"]],
> >   "more": false
> > }
> > ```

### PnL

Use PnL history to chart account profit and loss over the same interval. Each
point is the PnL realized inside its `interval` bucket — not a running total —
and buckets in which nothing was realized are omitted, so the series is
sparse.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const pnl = session.listPnlHistory({
>   interval: "1h",
>   start: Date.now() - 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
>   end: Date.now(),
> });
>
> for await (const page of pnl) {
>   // page.items: PerpsPnlPoint[]
> }
> ```
>
> Each page returns points you can plot as account PnL over time.
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsPnlPoint\[]
> >

> > [
> >   {
> >     "timestamp": 1767000000000,
> >     "pnl": "12.5"
> >   }
> > ]
> > ```

> [tab] Python
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
>
> end = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
> start = end - timedelta(days=7)
>

>     interval="1h",
>     start=start,

>     # page.items: tuple[PerpsPnlPoint, ...]
>     pass
> ```
>
> Each page returns points you can plot as account PnL over time.
>
> > [accordion] Output: tuple\[PerpsPnlPoint, ...]
> >
> > ```json theme={null}
> > [
> >   {
> >     "timestamp": 1767000000000,
> >     "pnl": "12.5"
> >   }
> > ]
> > ```

> [tab] API
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl -G "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/account/pnl" \

# Authenticated Sessions
Source: https://docs.polymarket.com/perps/authenticated-sessions

Set up authenticated access for Perps trading and account data

An authenticated session is a two-way authenticated communication channel with
the Perps system that allows your app to place orders, read private Perps account
data, and receive private real-time updates.

## Check Registration

Check whether an address already has a Perps account before setting up private
access. This lookup is public and does not create an account or credentials.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Use `fetchPerpsRegistration()` on a `PublicClient` or `SecureClient`. This example
> creates a public client and checks the account owner's address.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { createPublicClient } from "@polymarket/client";
>
> const publicClient = createPublicClient();
> const registered = await publicClient.fetchPerpsRegistration({
>   address: "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
> });
> // registered: boolean
> ```

> [tab] Python
>
> Use `fetch_perps_registration()` on an `AsyncPublicClient` or `AsyncSecureClient`.
> This example creates a public client and checks the account owner's address.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from polymarket import AsyncPublicClient
>
> async with AsyncPublicClient() as public_client:
>     registered = await public_client.fetch_perps_registration(
>         address="0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111"
>     )
>     # registered: bool
> ```

> [tab] API
>
> Send the account owner's address to the public registration endpoint. No
> authentication headers are required.
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl --get "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/info/registered" \
>   --data-urlencode "address=0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111"
> ```
>
> An example response for an address without a Perps account is:
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "registered": false
> }
> ```

A positive result means the address has a Perps account. Registration is
permanent. A negative result can be cached for up to ten seconds, so a newly
registered account may not appear immediately. Registration alone does not
confirm that credentials are valid or that the account has collateral available.

## Set Up Perps Access

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> **1. Create a Secure Client**
>
> Create a `SecureClient` for the Polymarket wallet that owns the Perps account,
> using the signer that controls it.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { createSecureClient } from "@polymarket/client";
> import { privateKey } from "@polymarket/client/viem";
>
> const client = await createSecureClient({
>   wallet: process.env.POLYMARKET_WALLET_ADDRESS!,
>   signer: privateKey(process.env.PRIVATE_KEY!),
> });
> ```
>
> > [!NOTE]
> >
> > This example uses Viem for wallet signing. See the [TypeScript tooling
> > guide](/getting-started/typescript#wallet-integrations) for other wallet
> > library integrations.
>
> **2. Open a Perps Session**
>
> Open a Perps session. By default, delegated Perps credentials expire after one
> week.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const session = await client.openPerpsSession();
> ```
>
> You can also set the session lifetime and label explicitly. `expiresIn` is
> measured in milliseconds.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const session = await client.openPerpsSession({
>   expiresIn: 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
>   label: "trading-app",
> });
> ```

> [tab] Python
>
> **1. Create a Secure Client**
>
> Create an `AsyncSecureClient` for the Polymarket wallet that owns the Perps
> account, using the signer that controls it.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import os
>
> from polymarket import AsyncSecureClient
>
> client = await AsyncSecureClient.create(
>     private_key=os.environ["PRIVATE_KEY"],
>     wallet=os.environ["POLYMARKET_WALLET_ADDRESS"],
> )
> ```
>
> **2. Open a Perps Session**
>
> Open a Perps session. By default, delegated Perps credentials expire after one
> week.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> session = await client.open_perps_session()
> ```
>
> You can also set the session lifetime and label explicitly. `expires_in` is a
> `timedelta`.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from datetime import timedelta
>
> session = await client.open_perps_session(
>     expires_in=timedelta(days=7),
>     label="trading-app",
> )
> ```

> [tab] API
>
> Start by registering new proxy credentials for an existing Polymarket account.
> If you do not have one yet, create an account at
> [polymarket.com](https://polymarket.com) first.
>
> **1. Generate a Proxy Signer**
>
> Generate a fresh keypair for the proxy signer. Perps uses this key to authorize
> trading operations on behalf of the Polymarket account signer, without requiring
> the account signer to sign every order.
>
> Use any secure EVM key-generation flow.
>
> ```bash Foundry theme={null}
> $ cast wallet new
> Successfully created new keypair.
> Address: <proxy_address>
> Private key: <proxy_private_key>
> ```
>
> ```ts Viem theme={null}
> import { generatePrivateKey, privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
>
> const privateKey = generatePrivateKey();
> const { address } = privateKeyToAccount(privateKey);
> ```
>
> Store the private key securely. It will be used to sign Perps trading operations
> for the Polymarket account signer.
>
> **2. Create Proxy Typed Data**
>
> Create an EIP-712 `CreateProxy` payload.
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "domain": {
>     "name": "Polymarket",
>     "version": "1",
>     "chainId": 137
>   },
>   "primaryType": "CreateProxy",
>   "types": {
>     "CreateProxy": [
>       { "name": "addr", "type": "address" },
>       { "name": "exp", "type": "uint64" },
>       { "name": "salt", "type": "uint64" },
>       { "name": "ts", "type": "uint64" }
>     ]
>   },
>   "message": {
>     "addr": "<proxy_address>",
>     "exp": 1767225600000,
>     "salt": 123456789,
>     "ts": 1767000000000
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> Use these values consistently in the typed data and request body.
>
> | Field | Value |
> | - | - |
> | `addr` | `<proxy_address>` from the previous step. |
> | `exp` | Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the proxy signer stops being valid. |
> | `ts` | Current Unix timestamp in milliseconds. |
> | `salt` | Random integer generated for this signed request. |
>
> **3. Sign Proxy Typed Data**
>
> Sign the `CreateProxy` typed data with the signer for the Polymarket account.
>
> ```ts Viem theme={null}
> import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
>
> const account = privateKeyToAccount("<polymarket_account_signer_private_key>");
>
> const signature = await account.signTypedData({
>   domain: {
>     name: "Polymarket",
>     version: "1",
>     chainId: 137,
>   },
>   primaryType: "CreateProxy",
>   types: {
>     CreateProxy: [
>       { name: "addr", type: "address" },
>       { name: "exp", type: "uint64" },
>       { name: "salt", type: "uint64" },
>       { name: "ts", type: "uint64" },
>     ],
>   },
>   message: {
>     addr: "<proxy_address>",
>     exp: 1767225600000,
>     salt: 123456789,
>     ts: 1767000000000,
>   },
> });
> ```
>
> **4. Authorize the Proxy Signer**
>
> Authorize the generated proxy signer for your Perps account.
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl -X POST "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/account/proxy" \
>   -H "content-type: application/json" \
>   -d '{
>     "op": {
>       "type": "createProxy",
>       "args": {
>         "owner": "<polymarket_account_signer_address>",
>         "proxy": "<proxy_address>",
>         "expiry": 1767225600000
>       }
>     },
>     "sig": "<signature>",
>     "salt": 123456789,
>     "ts": 1767000000000,
>     "label": "trading-app"
>   }'
> ```
>
> Map the request fields to the values from the previous steps.
>
> * `owner` is the signer address for the Polymarket account.
> * `proxy` is `<proxy_address>` from the first step.
> * `sig` is `<signature>` from the previous step.
> * `salt` and `ts` are the same values used in the typed data from step 2.
> * `label` is an identifier for this proxy credential instance.
>
> The response contains the proxy secret.
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "secret": "<proxy_secret>"
> }
> ```
>
> Store the proxy private key, proxy address, proxy secret, and expiry securely.

## Session Lifecycle

Open an authenticated session to start trading, read private Perps account data,
and receive private real-time updates.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> **1. Listen for Session Events**
>
> After opening a Perps session, iterate over it to receive private real-time
> updates.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const session = await client.openPerpsSession();
>
> for await (const event of session) {
>   switch (event.type) {
>     case "order":
>       // Update local order state.
>       break;
>
>     case "fill":
>       // Update position, PnL, or execution history.
>       break;
>
>     case "portfolio":
>       // Refresh margin, equity, and position views.
>       break;
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> This example handles a few common session events. `order` and `fill` are the
> core trading updates, while `portfolio` provides periodic account-level snapshots
> for margin, equity, positions, and withdrawable balance.
>
> See [Reconcile Trade State](/perps/trading#reconcile-trade-state) for how to use
> these events to keep local trading state in sync.
>
> **2. Close the Session**
>
> You can close the session at any time by calling `session.close()`. Closing a
> session releases local resources; stored credentials can still be resumed until
> they expire.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> for await (const event of session) {
>   if (shouldCloseSession) {
>     await session.close();
>     break;
>   }
>
>   // …
> }
> ```

> [tab] Python
>
> **1. Listen for Session Events**
>
> After opening a Perps session, iterate over it to receive private real-time
> updates.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> session = await client.open_perps_session()
>
> async for event in session:
>     if event.type == "order":
>         # Update local order state.
>         pass
>     elif event.type == "fill":
>         # Update position, PnL, or execution history.
>         pass
>     elif event.type == "portfolio":
>         # Refresh margin, equity, and position views.
>         pass
> ```
>
> This example handles a few common session events. `order` and `fill` are the
> core trading updates, while `portfolio` provides periodic account-level snapshots
> for margin, equity, positions, and withdrawable balance.
>
> See [Reconcile Trade State](/perps/trading#reconcile-trade-state) for how to use
> these events to keep local trading state in sync.
>
> **2. Close the Session**
>
> You can close the session at any time by calling `session.close()`. Closing a
> session releases local resources; stored credentials can still be resumed until
> they expire.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> async for event in session:
>     if should_close_session:
>         await session.close()
>         break
>
>     # …
> ```

> [tab] API
>
> **1. Authenticate a WebSocket Connection**
>
> Connect to the Perps WebSocket production URL.
>
> ```text theme={null}
> wss://ws.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/ws
> ```
>
> After the connection opens, send an authentication frame with the proxy address
> and proxy secret.
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "id": 1,
>   "req": "post",
>   "op": {
>     "type": "auth",
>     "args": {
>       "proxy": "<proxy_address>",
>       "secret": "<proxy_secret>"
>     }
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> Check the authentication response before subscribing to private channels.
>
> ```json Success theme={null}
> {
>   "id": 1,
>   "data": {
>     "status": "ok",
>     "pod": "gateway-ws-7b68c9d4f5-m2n8p"
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> ```json Failure theme={null}
> {
>   "id": 1,
>   "data": {
>     "status": "err",
>     "error": "<error_message>"
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> A successful acknowledgement includes `pod`, the identity of the gateway pod
> serving the connection. Record it with your connection logs so your activity
> can be matched against exchange logs. It is correlation metadata only — pods
> are not addressable, and a reconnect can land on a different pod. Treat the
> field as optional: older pods omit it during a rolling deploy, and failures
> never include it.
>
> **2. Handle Session Events**
>
> Authenticated WebSocket connections receive private session update frames. These
> examples show a few common events: `orders` and `fills` for trading activity,
> and `portfolio` for periodic account-level snapshots.
>
> ```json Order theme={null}
> {
>   "ch": "orders",
>   "ts": 1767225600000,
>   "ets": 1767225600000,
>   "sq": 1234567890,
>   "data": {
>     "oid": 1234567890,
>     "iid": 1,
>     "buy": true,
>     "p": "65000.00",
>     "qty": "0.01",
>     "tif": "gtc",
>     "po": false,
>     "status": "open",
>     "rest": "0.01",
>     "fill": "0",
>     "cts": 1767225600000,
>     "uts": 1767225600000
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> ```json Fill theme={null}
> {
>   "ch": "fills",
>   "ts": 1767225600000,
>   "ets": 1767225600000,
>   "sq": 1234567891,
>   "data": {
>     "tid": 987654321,
>     "oid": 1234567890,
>     "iid": 1,
>     "side": "long",
>     "p": "65000.00",
>     "qty": "0.01",
>     "taker": true,
>     "fee": "0.26",
>     "fea": "pUSD",
>     "psz": "0",
>     "pep": "0",
>     "pnl": "0",
>     "liq": false,
>     "adl": false,
>     "ts": 1767225600000
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> ```json Portfolio theme={null}
> {
>   "ch": "portfolio",
>   "ts": 1767225600000,
>   "ets": 1767225600000,
>   "sq": 1234567892,
>   "data": {
>     "positions": [],
>     "margin": {
>       "total_account_value": "10.00",
>       "available_order_margin": "10.00",
>       "total_initial_margin": "0",
>       "total_maintenance_margin": "0",
>       "total_position_value": "0"
>     },
>     "withdrawable": "10.00",
>     "in_liquidation": false,
>     "fee_tier": 0,
>     "timestamp": 1767225600000
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> These are examples of common session events, not the full event list.
> `ts` is the server send time. `ets` is the newest reflected event time, both in
> Unix milliseconds. An `ets` of `0` means the event horizon is unknown. Use `sq`
> for sequence-based reconciliation rather than treating send time as event order.
>
> **3. Keep the Connection Alive**
>
> Send an application-level ping from the client about every 25 seconds.
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "id": 0,
>   "req": "post",
>   "op": {
>     "type": "ping"
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> The server responds with a pong payload.
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "id": 0,
>   "data": {
>     "status": "ok",
>     "ts": 1767225600000,
>     "sq": 1234567890
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> Treat the connection as stale if no messages arrive for about 65 seconds.
>
> **4. Close the Connection**
>
> Close the WebSocket connection when the current workflow is finished. Closing the
> connection does not revoke the proxy credential.

## Resume a Session

Resume a session when stored credentials are still valid and a Perps workflow
needs to continue in a new runtime context.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Read `session.credentials` after opening a session and store the object in secure
> credential storage.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const credentials = session.credentials;
> // credentials: PerpsCredentials
> ```
>
> where `PerpsCredentials` is:
>
> ```ts PerpsCredentials Type theme={null}
> type PerpsCredentials = {
>   proxy: EvmAddress;
>   privateKey: PrivateKey;
>   secret: string;
>   expiresAt: number;
> };
> ```
>
> ```json PerpsCredentials Example theme={null}
> {
>   "proxy": "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
>   "privateKey": "0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222",
>   "secret": "<proxy_secret>",
>   "expiresAt": 1766725200000
> }
> ```
>
> Pass stored credentials back to `openPerpsSession()` while they are still valid.
> The SDK validates them and resumes the session.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const session = await client.openPerpsSession({
>   credentials,
> });
> // session: PerpsSession
> ```

> [tab] Python
>
> Read `session.credentials` after opening a session and store the object in secure
> credential storage.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> credentials = session.credentials
> # credentials: PerpsCredentials
> ```
>
> where `PerpsCredentials` is:
>
> ```python PerpsCredentials Type theme={null}
> from polymarket import PerpsCredentials
>
> # credentials: PerpsCredentials
> ```
>
> ```json PerpsCredentials Example theme={null}
> {
>   "proxy": "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
>   "private_key": "0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222",
>   "secret": "<proxy_secret>",
>   "expires_at": "2026-01-25T18:20:00Z"
> }
> ```
>
> For JSON-backed storage, serialize the model and keep the result encrypted.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> stored_credentials = credentials.model_dump(mode="json")
> ```
>
> Pass stored credentials back to `open_perps_session()` while they are still
> valid. The SDK validates them and resumes the session.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> from polymarket import PerpsCredentials
>
> credentials = PerpsCredentials.model_validate(stored_credentials)
>
> session = await client.open_perps_session(credentials=credentials)
> # session: PerpsSession
> ```

> [tab] API
>
> Resume an API session by reusing stored proxy credentials while they are still
> valid.
>
> Store the credential material from the setup flow in secure credential storage.
>
> | Field | Use it to |
> | - | - |
> | `<proxy_address>` | Identify the proxy credential. |
> | `<proxy_private_key>` | Sign Perps trading operations. |
> | `<proxy_secret>` | Authenticate private REST and real-time access. |
> | `expiry` | Know when to register a new proxy credential. |
>
> For private REST reads, pass the proxy address and proxy secret as headers.
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/account/portfolio" \
>   -H "polymarket-proxy: <proxy_address>" \
>   -H "polymarket-secret: <proxy_secret>"
> ```
>
> For a new WebSocket connection, send the same authentication frame used when the
> session was opened.
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "id": 1,
>   "req": "post",
>   "op": {
>     "type": "auth",
>     "args": {
>       "proxy": "<proxy_address>",
>       "secret": "<proxy_secret>"
>     }
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> If the credential has expired, register a new proxy credential before resuming
> private workflows.


# Builder Codes
Source: https://docs.polymarket.com/perps/builder-codes

Earn builder fees for routing orders and building new Polymarket Perps experiences

Builder Attribution lets applications earn an additional fee for routing Perps
orders with a fee explicitly approved by the trader.

The **Builder** operates the application and receives the fee in its Perps
account. The **Trader** places orders through that application and approves the
Builder fee.

## Quickstart: Place an order with Builder Attribution

Use the Trader's [funded Perps account](/perps/fund-your-account) and owner signer
to approve the Builder fee once, then place attributed orders. Approval remains
valid across sessions until revoked or replaced.

Each Builder is identified by its Perps account address. The Builder and Trader
must be different accounts.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Use `createSecureClient()` from `@polymarket/client` with the Trader's owner
> signer. This example uses Viem. See
> [Wallet Integrations](/getting-started/typescript#wallet-integrations) for other
> signer providers. Set `builderAddress` to the Builder's EVM account address and
> `instrumentId` to the instrument selected in [Prepare a Trade](/perps/trading#prepare-a-trade).
>
> **1. Create a Secure Client**
>
> Create a `SecureClient` for the Trader. Set `POLYMARKET_WALLET_ADDRESS` to the
> Polymarket wallet that owns the Perps account and `PRIVATE_KEY` to its owner's
> signing key.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { createSecureClient } from "@polymarket/client";
> import { privateKey } from "@polymarket/client/viem";
>
> const client = await createSecureClient({
>   wallet: process.env.POLYMARKET_WALLET_ADDRESS!,
>   signer: privateKey(process.env.PRIVATE_KEY!),
> });
> ```
>
> **2. Open a Trader Session**
>
> Call `client.openPerpsSession()` with the Builder's account address:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const session = await client.openPerpsSession({
>   builderAttribution: builderAddress,
> });
> ```
>
> **3. Approve the Builder Fee**
>
> Call `session.approveBuilderFee` with an explicit `maxFeeRate` before the Trader's
> first attributed order. Skip this step if the Trader already has an active approval:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> await session.approveBuilderFee({ maxFeeRate: "0.001" });
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsBuilderApproval
> >
> > ```ts PerpsBuilderApproval Type theme={null}
> > type PerpsBuilderApproval = {
> >   trader: EvmAddress;
> >   builder: EvmAddress;
> >   maxFeeRate: DecimalString; // Zero revokes consent
> >   approvalVersion: number;
> >   timestamp: EpochMilliseconds;
> >   sequence: number;
> > };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json PerpsBuilderApproval Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "trader": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678",
> >   "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
> >   "maxFeeRate": "0.001",
> >   "approvalVersion": 1,
> >   "timestamp": 1767000000000,
> >   "sequence": 1234567889
> > }
> > ```
>
> **4. Place an Attributed Order**
>
> Call `session.placeOrder()` to submit an immediate-or-cancel buy using the
> session's Builder:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { OrderSide, PerpsTimeInForce } from "@polymarket/client";
>
> const result = await session.placeOrder({
>   instrumentId,
>   side: OrderSide.BUY,
>   quantity: "0.01",
>   timeInForce: PerpsTimeInForce.IOC,
> });
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: PlacePerpsOrderResult
> >
> > ```ts PlacePerpsOrderResult Type theme={null}
> > type PlacePerpsOrderResult = {
> >   order: PerpsOrder;
> > };
> >
> > type PerpsOrder = {
> >   id: PerpsOrderId;
> >   instrumentId: PerpsInstrumentId;
> >   side: OrderSide;
> >   price: DecimalString;
> >   quantity: DecimalString;
> >   timeInForce: PerpsTimeInForce;
> >   postOnly: boolean;
> >   reduceOnly: boolean;
> >   status: PerpsOrderStatus;
> >   restingQuantity: DecimalString;
> >   filledQuantity: DecimalString;
> >   createdTimestamp: EpochMilliseconds;
> >   updatedTimestamp: EpochMilliseconds;
> >   clientOrderId: string | undefined;
> >   tpSl: PerpsTpSlOrderFields | undefined;
> >   builder?: PerpsBuilderTerms;
> > };
> >
> > type PerpsBuilderTerms = {
> >   address: EvmAddress;
> >   feeRate: DecimalString;
> > };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json PlacePerpsOrderResult Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "order": {
> >     "id": 67890,
> >     "instrumentId": 1,
> >     "side": "BUY",
> >     "price": "65000",
> >     "quantity": "0.01",
> >     "timeInForce": "ioc",
> >     "postOnly": false,
> >     "reduceOnly": false,
> >     "status": "filled",
> >     "restingQuantity": "0",
> >     "filledQuantity": "0.01",
> >     "createdTimestamp": 1767000010000,
> >     "updatedTimestamp": 1767000010000,
> >     "builder": {
> >       "address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
> >       "feeRate": "0.001"
> >     }
> >   }
> > }
> > ```
>
> The session applies the same terms to single orders, batches, and generated
> take-profit and stop-loss exits. Await approval before submitting orders that
> should use its terms.

> [tab] Python
>
> Use `AsyncSecureClient` from `polymarket-client` and run the examples inside an async
> function. `builder_address` is your enabled Builder's account address.
> `instrument_id` identifies the instrument selected in
> [Prepare a Trade](/perps/trading#prepare-a-trade).
>
> **1. Create a Secure Client**
>
> Create an `AsyncSecureClient` for the Trader. Set `POLYMARKET_WALLET_ADDRESS`
> to the Polymarket wallet that owns the Perps account and `PRIVATE_KEY` to its
> owner's signing key.
>
> ```python theme={null}
> import os
>
> from polymarket import AsyncSecureClient
>
> client = await AsyncSecureClient.create(
>     private_key=os.environ["PRIVATE_KEY"],
>     wallet=os.environ["POLYMARKET_WALLET_ADDRESS"],
> )
> ```
>
> **2. Open a Trader Session**
>
> Call `client.open_perps_session()` with the Builder's account address:
>
> ```python theme={null}
> session = await client.open_perps_session(builder_attribution=builder_address)
> ```
>
> **3. Approve the Builder Fee**
>
> Call `session.approve_builder_fee` with an explicit `max_fee_rate` before the Trader's
> first attributed order. Skip this step if the Trader already has an active approval:
>
> ```python theme={null}
> await session.approve_builder_fee(max_fee_rate="0.001")
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsBuilderApproval
> >
> > ```python PerpsBuilderApproval Type theme={null}
> > class PerpsBuilderApproval:
> >     trader: EvmAddress
> >     builder: EvmAddress
> >     max_fee_rate: Decimal  # Zero revokes consent
> >     approval_version: int
> >     timestamp: datetime
> >     sequence: int
> > ```
> >
> > ```json PerpsBuilderApproval Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "trader": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678",
> >   "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
> >   "max_fee_rate": "0.001",
> >   "approval_version": 1,
> >   "timestamp": "2025-12-29T09:20:00Z",
> >   "sequence": 1234567889
> > }
> > ```
>
> **4. Place an Attributed Order**
>
> Call `session.place_order()` to submit an immediate-or-cancel buy using the
> session's Builder:
>
> ```python theme={null}
> result = await session.place_order(
>     instrument_id=instrument_id,
>     side="BUY",
>     quantity="0.01",
>     time_in_force="ioc",
> )
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsOrderPlacement
> >
> > ```python PerpsOrderPlacement Type theme={null}
> > class PerpsOrderPlacement:
> >     order: PerpsOrder
> >     tp_sl: PerpsPlacedTpSlOrders | None = None
> >
> >
> > class PerpsOrder:
> >     id: PerpsOrderId
> >     instrument_id: PerpsInstrumentId
> >     side: OrderSide
> >     price: Decimal
> >     quantity: Decimal
> >     time_in_force: PerpsTimeInForce
> >     post_only: bool
> >     reduce_only: bool
> >     status: PerpsOrderStatus
> >     resting_quantity: Decimal
> >     filled_quantity: Decimal
> >     created_at: datetime
> >     updated_at: datetime
> >     client_order_id: str | None = None
> >     tp_sl: PerpsTpSlOrderFields | None = None
> >     builder: PerpsBuilderAttribution | None = None
> >
> >
> > class PerpsBuilderAttribution:
> >     address: EvmAddress
> >     fee_rate: Decimal
> > ```
> >
> > ```json PerpsOrderPlacement Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "order": {
> >     "id": 67890,
> >     "instrument_id": 1,
> >     "side": "BUY",
> >     "price": "65000",
> >     "quantity": "0.01",
> >     "time_in_force": "ioc",
> >     "post_only": false,
> >     "reduce_only": false,
> >     "status": "filled",
> >     "resting_quantity": "0",
> >     "filled_quantity": "0.01",
> >     "builder": {
> >       "address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
> >       "fee_rate": "0.001"
> >     },
> >     "created_at": "2025-12-29T09:20:10Z",
> >     "updated_at": "2025-12-29T09:20:10Z"
> >   }
> > }
> > ```
>
> The session applies the same terms to single orders, batches, and generated
> take-profit and stop-loss exits. Await approval before submitting orders that
> should use its terms.

> [tab] API
>
> Use the account owner's signer for fee approval and a trading proxy for orders.
> Set up proxy credentials through [Authenticated
> Sessions](/perps/authenticated-sessions#set-up-perps-access) first. The examples
> below use the same signing flow as [Place Orders](/perps/trading#place-orders).
>
> **1. Read the Saved Approval**
>
> Fetch the Trader's grant using its proxy credentials:
>
> ```bash Request theme={null}
> curl -G "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/account/builder-approvals" \
>   -H "polymarket-proxy: <proxy_address>" \
>   -H "polymarket-secret: <proxy_secret>" \
>   --data-urlencode "builder=<builder_account_address>"
> ```
>
> ```ts BuilderApprovals Type theme={null}
> type BuilderApprovals = {
>   data: Array<{
>     trader: string;
>     builder: string;
>     max_fee_rate: string;
>     approval_version: number;
>     timestamp: number;
>     sequence: number;
>   }>;
> };
> ```
>
> ```json BuilderApprovals Example theme={null}
> {
>   "data": []
> }
> ```
>
> The response's `data` array includes revoked grants. Use the saved
> `approval_version` plus one, or `1` if no grant exists.
>
> **2. Build the Approval Operation**
>
> Read the Builder's configured fee for this approval:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const builderAddress = "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234";
> const builderStatusResponse = await fetch(
>   `https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/info/builder?address=${builderAddress}`,
> );
> const builderStatus = await builderStatusResponse.json();
> const builderFeeRate = builderStatus.max_fee_rate;
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: BuilderStatus
> >
> > ```ts BuilderStatus Type theme={null}
> > type BuilderStatus = {
> >   address: string;
> >   registered: boolean;
> >   enabled: boolean;
> >   admission_enabled: boolean;
> >   max_fee_rate: string;
> > };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json BuilderStatus Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
> >   "registered": true,
> >   "enabled": true,
> >   "admission_enabled": true,
> >   "max_fee_rate": "0.001"
> > }
> > ```
>
> Use `builderFeeRate` as `<builder_fee_rate>` below and the saved approval
> version plus one as `approval_version`. This example uses `1` for the first
> grant. The account owner signs these terms:
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "type": "approveBuilder",
>   "args": {
>     "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>     "max_fee_rate": "<builder_fee_rate>",
>     "approval_version": 1
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> **3. Create the Approval Hash**
>
> MessagePack-encode the compact approval operation, then hash the bytes with
> `keccak256`. This example uses `@msgpack/msgpack` and Viem:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { encode } from "@msgpack/msgpack";
> import { keccak256 } from "viem";
>
> const approvalOperation = [
>   "approveBuilder",
>   [builderAddress, builderFeeRate, 1],
> ];
> const approvalHash = keccak256(encode(approvalOperation));
> ```
>
> The address, rate, and version must match the structured operation above.
>
> **4. Create Approval Typed Data**
>
> Create an EIP-712 `Op` payload using the operation hash:
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "domain": {
>     "name": "Polymarket",
>     "version": "1",
>     "chainId": 137
>   },
>   "primaryType": "Op",
>   "types": {
>     "Op": [
>       {
>         "name": "data",
>         "type": "bytes32"
>       },
>       {
>         "name": "salt",
>         "type": "uint64"
>       },
>       {
>         "name": "ts",
>         "type": "uint64"
>       }
>     ]
>   },
>   "message": {
>     "data": "<approval_hash>",
>     "salt": 123456789,
>     "ts": 1767000000000
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> Replace the sample `salt` with a fresh random integer and `ts` with the current
> Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Use those same values when signing and submitting
> the request. The production signing domain uses `chainId: 137`.
>
> **5. Sign Approval Typed Data**
>
> Sign with the account owner's key using Viem. Set `OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY` to that
> key before running the example:
>
> ```ts Viem theme={null}
> import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
>
> const account = privateKeyToAccount(
>   process.env.OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY as `0x${string}`,
> );
> const approvalSignature = await account.signTypedData({
>   domain: { name: "Polymarket", version: "1", chainId: 137 },
>   primaryType: "Op",
>   types: {
>     Op: [
>       { name: "data", type: "bytes32" },
>       { name: "salt", type: "uint64" },
>       { name: "ts", type: "uint64" },
>     ],
>   },
>   message: {
>     data: approvalHash,
>     salt: 123456789n,
>     ts: 1767000000000n,
>   },
> });
> ```
>
> **6. Submit the Approval**
>
> Submit the operation with `approvalSignature` as `<approval_signature>` and the
> same salt and timestamp used in the signed typed data:
>
> ```bash Request theme={null}
> curl -X POST "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/account/builder-approvals" \
>   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -d '{
>     "op": {
>       "type": "approveBuilder",
>       "args": {
>         "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>         "max_fee_rate": "<builder_fee_rate>",
>         "approval_version": 1
>       }
>     },
>     "sig": "<approval_signature>",
>     "salt": 123456789,
>     "ts": 1767000000000
>   }'
> ```
>
> ```ts BuilderApproval Type theme={null}
> type BuilderApproval = {
>   trader: string;
>   builder: string;
>   max_fee_rate: string;
>   approval_version: number;
>   timestamp: number;
>   sequence: number;
> };
> ```
>
> ```json BuilderApproval Example theme={null}
> {
>   "trader": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678",
>   "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>   "max_fee_rate": "0.001",
>   "approval_version": 1,
>   "timestamp": 1767000000000,
>   "sequence": 1234567889
> }
> ```
>
> The response contains the committed `approval_version`, `max_fee_rate`, and
> `sequence`. Check that its Builder, rate, and version match the request before
> placing an order. If the result is unclear, read the saved grant before signing
> a replacement.
>
> **7. Build the Order Operation**
>
> Choose an instrument, price, and quantity as shown in
> [Prepare a Trade](/perps/trading#prepare-a-trade). This example places an
> immediate-or-cancel buy with a limit price of `65000` and the Builder fee
> approved above:
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "type": "createOrders",
>   "args": [
>     {
>       "iid": 1,
>       "buy": true,
>       "p": "65000",
>       "qty": "0.01",
>       "tif": "ioc",
>       "po": false,
>       "c": "7f9e4a2b6c8d0e1f1234567890abcdef",
>       "builder": {
>         "address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>         "fee_rate": "<builder_fee_rate>"
>       }
>     }
>   ]
> }
> ```
>
> **8. Create the Order Hash**
>
> Append the Builder tuple after the existing order fields, then omit undefined
> optional entries before MessagePack encoding. Use the same values as the order
> operation above:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { encode } from "@msgpack/msgpack";
> import { keccak256 } from "viem";
>
> const signableOrder = [
>   "createOrders",
>   [
>     [
>       1,
>       true,
>       "65000",
>       "0.01",
>       "ioc",
>       false,
>       undefined, // ro
>       "7f9e4a2b6c8d0e1f1234567890abcdef",
>       undefined, // tr
>       undefined, // gtt
>       [builderAddress, builderFeeRate],
>     ].filter((value) => value !== undefined),
>   ],
> ];
> const orderHash = keccak256(encode(signableOrder));
> ```
>
> **9. Create Order Typed Data**
>
> Create an EIP-712 `Op` payload using the operation hash:
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "domain": {
>     "name": "Polymarket",
>     "version": "1",
>     "chainId": 137
>   },
>   "primaryType": "Op",
>   "types": {
>     "Op": [
>       {
>         "name": "data",
>         "type": "bytes32"
>       },
>       {
>         "name": "salt",
>         "type": "uint64"
>       },
>       {
>         "name": "ts",
>         "type": "uint64"
>       }
>     ]
>   },
>   "message": {
>     "data": "<order_hash>",
>     "salt": 234567890,
>     "ts": 1767000010000
>   }
> }
> ```
>
> Replace the sample `salt` with a fresh random integer and `ts` with the current
> Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Use those same values when signing and submitting
> the request. The production signing domain uses `chainId: 137`.
>
> **10. Sign Order Typed Data**
>
> Sign with the trading proxy's key using Viem. Set `PROXY_PRIVATE_KEY` to that
> key before running the example:
>
> ```ts Viem theme={null}
> import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
>
> const account = privateKeyToAccount(
>   process.env.PROXY_PRIVATE_KEY as `0x${string}`,
> );
> const orderSignature = await account.signTypedData({
>   domain: { name: "Polymarket", version: "1", chainId: 137 },
>   primaryType: "Op",
>   types: {
>     Op: [
>       { name: "data", type: "bytes32" },
>       { name: "salt", type: "uint64" },
>       { name: "ts", type: "uint64" },
>     ],
>   },
>   message: {
>     data: orderHash,
>     salt: 234567890n,
>     ts: 1767000010000n,
>   },
> });
> ```
>
> **11. Submit the Order**
>
> Submit `orderSignature` as `<order_signature>`, keeping the operation, salt, and
> timestamp identical to the signed values:
>
> ```bash Request theme={null}
> curl -X POST "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/trade/orders" \
>   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -d '{
>     "op": {
>       "type": "createOrders",
>       "args": [
>         {
>           "iid": 1,
>           "buy": true,
>           "p": "65000",
>           "qty": "0.01",
>           "tif": "ioc",
>           "po": false,
>           "c": "7f9e4a2b6c8d0e1f1234567890abcdef",
>           "builder": {
>             "address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>             "fee_rate": "<builder_fee_rate>"
>           }
>         }
>       ]
>     },
>     "sig": "<order_signature>",
>     "salt": 234567890,
>     "ts": 1767000010000
>   }'
> ```
>
> ```ts OrderResponse Type theme={null}
> type OrderResponse = {
>   status: "ok";
>   oid: number;
>   coid?: string;
>   builder?: {
>     address: string;
>     fee_rate: string;
>   };
> } | {
>   status: "err";
>   error: string;
>   oid?: number;
>   coid?: string;
> };
> ```
>
> ```json OrderResponse Example theme={null}
> [
>   {
>     "status": "ok",
>     "oid": 67890,
>     "coid": "7f9e4a2b6c8d0e1f1234567890abcdef",
>     "builder": {
>       "address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>       "fee_rate": "0.001"
>     }
>   }
> ]
> ```
>
> Check each result in the response array. `status: "ok"` confirms acceptance and
> `oid` identifies the order. `status: "err"` includes the rejection in `error`.
> Acceptance does not confirm execution.
>
> **12. Check the Order State**
>
> Use the returned `oid` to read the order with the Trader's proxy credentials:
>
> ```bash Request theme={null}
> curl -G "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/account/orders" \
>   -H "polymarket-proxy: <proxy_address>" \
>   -H "polymarket-secret: <proxy_secret>" \
>   --data-urlencode "order_id=<oid>"
> ```
>
> ```ts OrderData Type theme={null}
> type OrderData = {
>   order_id: number;
>   instrument_id: number;
>   buy: boolean;
>   price: string;
>   quantity: string;
>   tif: "gtc" | "ioc" | "fok";
>   post_only: boolean;
>   ro: boolean;
>   resting_quantity: string;
>   filled_quantity: string;
>   status: string;
>   created_timestamp: number;
>   updated_timestamp: number;
>   client_order_id?: string;
>   tpsl?: {
>     kind: "tp" | "sl";
>     scope: "order" | "position";
>     trp: string;
>     parent_oid?: number;
>     armed_qty?: string;
>     slip_bps?: number;
>   };
>   builder?: {
>     address: string;
>     fee_rate: string;
>   };
> };
> ```
>
> ```json OrderData Example theme={null}
> [
>   {
>     "order_id": 67890,
>     "instrument_id": 1,
>     "buy": true,
>     "price": "65000",
>     "quantity": "0.01",
>     "tif": "ioc",
>     "post_only": false,
>     "ro": false,
>     "status": "filled",
>     "resting_quantity": "0",
>     "filled_quantity": "0.01",
>     "created_timestamp": 1767000010000,
>     "updated_timestamp": 1767000010000,
>     "client_order_id": "7f9e4a2b6c8d0e1f1234567890abcdef",
>     "builder": {
>       "address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>       "fee_rate": "0.001"
>     }
>   }
> ]
> ```
>
> Read `status`, `filled_quantity`, and `resting_quantity` to determine the
> execution outcome. Full order reads include the saved `builder` terms.
> If the snapshot is not available yet, retry the read or follow private order
> updates through [Authenticated Sessions](/perps/authenticated-sessions#session-lifecycle).

## Trader Operations

Read and manage the Trader's consent, place attributed orders, and inspect the
fees charged on executions.

### Fetch Trader Approval

Check whether the Trader has already approved a Builder and the maximum fee
they accepted. Read the saved approval before asking for consent again. A
revoked approval remains in the account's history with a zero fee limit.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Call `session.fetchBuilderApprovals()` on the Trader's existing `PerpsSession`,
> filtering by the Builder's account address:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const approvals = await session.fetchBuilderApprovals({
>   builder: builderAddress,
> });
> const approval = approvals[0];
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsBuilderApproval\[]
> >
> > ```ts PerpsBuilderApproval Type theme={null}
> > type PerpsBuilderApproval = {
> >   trader: EvmAddress;
> >   builder: EvmAddress;
> >   maxFeeRate: DecimalString; // Zero revokes consent
> >   approvalVersion: number;
> >   timestamp: EpochMilliseconds;
> >   sequence: number;
> > };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json PerpsBuilderApproval Example theme={null}
> > [
> >   {
> >     "trader": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678",
> >     "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
> >     "maxFeeRate": "0.001",
> >     "approvalVersion": 1,
> >     "timestamp": 1767000000000,
> >     "sequence": 1234567889
> >   }
> > ]
> > ```
>
> An empty array means the Trader has no saved approval for this Builder.
> Otherwise, `approval.maxFeeRate` is the approved fee limit as a decimal string.
> Zero means consent was revoked. Compare the intended Builder fee with this
> limit to decide whether to request approval. `approval.approvalVersion` is the
> saved version, including after revocation.
>
> Omit the `builder` filter to fetch all of the Trader's saved Builder approvals.

> [tab] Python
>
> Call `session.fetch_builder_approvals()` on the Trader's existing `PerpsSession`,
> filtering by the Builder's account address:
>
> ```python theme={null}
> approvals = await session.fetch_builder_approvals(builder=builder_address)
> approval = approvals[0] if approvals else None
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: tuple\[PerpsBuilderApproval, …]
> >
> > ```python PerpsBuilderApproval Type theme={null}
> > class PerpsBuilderApproval:
> >     trader: EvmAddress
> >     builder: EvmAddress
> >     max_fee_rate: Decimal  # Zero revokes consent
> >     approval_version: int
> >     timestamp: datetime
> >     sequence: int
> > ```
> >
> > ```json PerpsBuilderApproval Example theme={null}
> > [
> >   {
> >     "trader": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678",
> >     "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
> >     "max_fee_rate": "0.001",
> >     "approval_version": 1,
> >     "timestamp": "2025-12-29T09:20:00Z",
> >     "sequence": 1234567889
> >   }
> > ]
> > ```
>
> An empty tuple means the Trader has no saved approval for this Builder.
> Otherwise, `approval.max_fee_rate` is the approved fee limit as a `Decimal`.
> Zero means consent was revoked. Compare the intended Builder fee with this
> limit to decide whether to request approval. `approval.approval_version` is the
> saved version, including after revocation.
>
> Omit the `builder` filter to fetch all of the Trader's saved Builder approvals.

> [tab] API
>
> Fetch the Trader's saved approval for the Builder using the Trader's proxy
> credentials:
>
> ```bash Request theme={null}
> curl -G "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/account/builder-approvals" \
>   -H "polymarket-proxy: <proxy_address>" \
>   -H "polymarket-secret: <proxy_secret>" \
>   --data-urlencode "builder=<builder_account_address>"
> ```
>
> ```ts BuilderApprovals Type theme={null}
> type BuilderApprovals = {
>   data: Array<{
>     trader: string;
>     builder: string;
>     max_fee_rate: string;
>     approval_version: number;
>     timestamp: number;
>     sequence: number;
>   }>;
> };
> ```
>
> ```json BuilderApprovals Example theme={null}
> {
>   "data": [
>     {
>       "trader": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678",
>       "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>       "max_fee_rate": "0.001",
>       "approval_version": 1,
>       "timestamp": 1767000000000,
>       "sequence": 1234567889
>     }
>   ]
> }
> ```
>
> An empty `data` array means the Trader has no saved approval for this Builder.
> Otherwise, `max_fee_rate` is the approved fee limit. `"0"` means consent was
> revoked. Compare the intended `builder.fee_rate` with this limit to decide
> whether to request approval. `approval_version` is the saved version, including
> after revocation. Omit the `builder` query parameter to fetch all saved Builder
> approvals for the authenticated Trader.
>
> Check whether the Builder can currently receive attributed orders:
>
> ```bash Request theme={null}
> curl -G "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/info/builder" \
>   --data-urlencode "address=<builder_account_address>"
> ```
>
> ```ts BuilderStatus Type theme={null}
> type BuilderStatus = {
>   address: string;
>   registered: boolean;
>   enabled: boolean;
>   admission_enabled: boolean;
>   max_fee_rate: string;
> };
> ```
>
> ```json BuilderStatus Example theme={null}
> {
>   "address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>   "registered": true,
>   "enabled": true,
>   "admission_enabled": true,
>   "max_fee_rate": "0.001"
> }
> ```
>
> Require `registered`, `enabled`, and `admission_enabled` to be `true`. The order's
> `builder.fee_rate` must be covered by both the Builder's current configuration
> and the Trader's positive approval. Fetching these values does not create or
> change consent. The server validates them again when it receives an order.

### Grant Approval

Approve the Builder fee once before placing attributed orders. Existing approval
remains valid across sessions until revoked or replaced. To approve a changed
Builder fee, grant approval again.

> [!WARNING]
>
> The maximum Builder fee is currently 10 basis points (0.1%). This limit may
> change in the future.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Call `session.approveBuilderFee` on a Trader session opened with
> `builderAttribution`. Pass the maximum fee the Trader agrees to authorize:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> await session.approveBuilderFee({ maxFeeRate: "0.001" });
> ```
>
> `maxFeeRate` is required and has no default. This example approves 10 basis points
> (0.1%). To select a Builder when the session has none, or approve a different
> Builder, also pass its address:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> await session.approveBuilderFee({
>   builderAddress,
>   maxFeeRate: "0.001",
> });
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsBuilderApproval
> >
> > ```ts PerpsBuilderApproval Type theme={null}
> > type PerpsBuilderApproval = {
> >   trader: EvmAddress;
> >   builder: EvmAddress;
> >   maxFeeRate: DecimalString; // Zero revokes consent
> >   approvalVersion: number;
> >   timestamp: EpochMilliseconds;
> >   sequence: number;
> > };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json PerpsBuilderApproval Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "trader": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678",
> >   "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
> >   "maxFeeRate": "0.001",
> >   "approvalVersion": 1,
> >   "timestamp": 1767000000000,
> >   "sequence": 1234567889
> > }
> > ```
>
> After confirmation, the session refreshes the Builder cap and uses the lower of
> that cap and the approved maximum for new orders.

> [tab] Python
>
> Call `session.approve_builder_fee` on a Trader session opened with
> `builder_attribution`. Pass the maximum fee the Trader agrees to authorize:
>
> ```python theme={null}
> await session.approve_builder_fee(max_fee_rate="0.001")
> ```
>
> `max_fee_rate` is required and has no default. This example approves 10 basis points
> (0.1%). To select a Builder when the session has none, or approve a different
> Builder, also pass its address:
>
> ```python theme={null}
> await session.approve_builder_fee(
>     builder_address=builder_address,
>     max_fee_rate="0.001",
> )
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsBuilderApproval
> >
> > ```python PerpsBuilderApproval Type theme={null}
> > class PerpsBuilderApproval:
> >     trader: EvmAddress
> >     builder: EvmAddress
> >     max_fee_rate: Decimal  # Zero revokes consent
> >     approval_version: int
> >     timestamp: datetime
> >     sequence: int
> > ```
> >
> > ```json PerpsBuilderApproval Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "trader": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678",
> >   "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
> >   "max_fee_rate": "0.001",
> >   "approval_version": 1,
> >   "timestamp": "2025-12-29T09:20:00Z",
> >   "sequence": 1234567889
> > }
> > ```
>
> After confirmation, the session refreshes the Builder cap and uses the lower of
> that cap and the approved maximum for new orders.

> [tab] API
>
> Use the owner-signed `approveBuilder` operation shown in the approval workflow
> above. Read the saved grant first and set `approval_version` to its current
> version plus one, or `1` for the first grant. Sign and submit the same Builder
> address, fee, and version.

### Revoke Approval

Revoke permission for new attributed orders. Existing accepted orders, including pending conditional orders,
retain their saved fees. Cancel those orders to prevent further charges.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Call `session.revokeBuilderFee()` with the Builder's account address:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> await session.revokeBuilderFee(builderAddress);
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsBuilderApproval
> >
> > ```ts PerpsBuilderApproval Type theme={null}
> > type PerpsBuilderApproval = {
> >   trader: EvmAddress;
> >   builder: EvmAddress;
> >   maxFeeRate: DecimalString; // Zero revokes consent
> >   approvalVersion: number;
> >   timestamp: EpochMilliseconds;
> >   sequence: number;
> > };
> > ```
> >
> > ```json PerpsBuilderApproval Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "trader": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678",
> >   "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
> >   "maxFeeRate": "0",
> >   "approvalVersion": 2,
> >   "timestamp": 1767000030000,
> >   "sequence": 1234567891
> > }
> > ```

> [tab] Python
>
> Call `session.revoke_builder_fee()` with the Builder's account address:
>
> ```python theme={null}
> await session.revoke_builder_fee(builder_address)
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsBuilderApproval
> >
> > ```python PerpsBuilderApproval Type theme={null}
> > class PerpsBuilderApproval:
> >     trader: EvmAddress
> >     builder: EvmAddress
> >     max_fee_rate: Decimal  # Zero revokes consent
> >     approval_version: int
> >     timestamp: datetime
> >     sequence: int
> > ```
> >
> > ```json PerpsBuilderApproval Example theme={null}
> > {
> >   "trader": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678",
> >   "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
> >   "max_fee_rate": "0",
> >   "approval_version": 2,
> >   "timestamp": "2025-12-29T09:20:30Z",
> >   "sequence": 1234567891
> > }
> > ```

> [tab] API
>
> Use the Trader account owner's signer to replace the saved approval with a
> zero maximum rate.
>
> **1. Read the Current Version**
>
> Fetch the latest grant, including its retained version if already revoked:
>
> ```bash Request theme={null}
> curl -G "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/account/builder-approvals" \
>   -H "polymarket-proxy: <proxy_address>" \
>   -H "polymarket-secret: <proxy_secret>" \
>   --data-urlencode "builder=<builder_account_address>"
> ```
>
> ```ts BuilderApprovals Type theme={null}
> type BuilderApprovals = {
>   data: Array<{
>     trader: string;
>     builder: string;
>     max_fee_rate: string;
>     approval_version: number;
>     timestamp: number;
>     sequence: number;
>   }>;
> };
> ```
>
> ```json BuilderApprovals Example theme={null}
> {
>   "data": [
>     {
>       "trader": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678",
>       "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>       "max_fee_rate": "0.001",
>       "approval_version": 1,
>       "timestamp": 1767000000000,
>       "sequence": 1234567889
>     }
>   ]
> }
> ```
>
> Use the returned `approval_version` plus one in the next step. The example uses `2` for a grant whose current version is `1`.
>
> **2. Create the Revocation Hash**
>
> Set the rate to `"0"` and use the next saved version. Hash the compact operation:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { encode } from "@msgpack/msgpack";
> import { keccak256 } from "viem";
>
> const revocationOperation = [
>   "approveBuilder",
>   ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234", "0", 2],
> ];
> const revocationHash = keccak256(encode(revocationOperation));
> ```
>
> **3. Create Revocation Typed Data**
>
> Use the same EIP-712 `Op` structure shown in the approval workflow. Set `data`
> to `revocationHash` and generate a new random salt and current Unix-millisecond
> timestamp. The next examples use sample values that you must replace in both
> the signature and the request.
>
> **4. Sign Revocation Typed Data**
>
> Sign with the account owner's key using Viem. Set `OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY` to that
> key before running the example:
>
> ```ts Viem theme={null}
> import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
>
> const account = privateKeyToAccount(
>   process.env.OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY as `0x${string}`,
> );
> const revocationSignature = await account.signTypedData({
>   domain: { name: "Polymarket", version: "1", chainId: 137 },
>   primaryType: "Op",
>   types: {
>     Op: [
>       { name: "data", type: "bytes32" },
>       { name: "salt", type: "uint64" },
>       { name: "ts", type: "uint64" },
>     ],
>   },
>   message: {
>     data: revocationHash,
>     salt: 456789012n,
>     ts: 1767000030000n,
>   },
> });
> ```
>
> **5. Submit the Revocation**
>
> Submit `revocationSignature` as `<revocation_signature>` with the matching
> operation, salt, and timestamp:
>
> ```bash Request theme={null}
> curl -X POST "https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1/account/builder-approvals" \
>   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -d '{
>     "op": {
>       "type": "approveBuilder",
>       "args": {
>         "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>         "max_fee_rate": "0",
>         "approval_version": 2
>       }
>     },
>     "sig": "<revocation_signature>",
>     "salt": 456789012,
>     "ts": 1767000030000
>   }'
> ```
>
> ```ts BuilderApproval Type theme={null}
> type BuilderApproval = {
>   trader: string;
>   builder: string;
>   max_fee_rate: string;
>   approval_version: number;
>   timestamp: number;
>   sequence: number;
> };
> ```
>
> ```json BuilderApproval Example theme={null}
> {
>   "trader": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678",
>   "builder": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>   "max_fee_rate": "0",
>   "approval_version": 2,
>   "timestamp": 1767000030000,
>   "sequence": 1234567891
> }
> ```
>
> Existing orders, including pending conditional orders, keep their saved fees.
> Cancel them to prevent further charges.
>
> Check that the response has `max_fee_rate: "0"` and the version you submitted.
> Stale or replayed versions are rejected. If the result is unclear, read the
> saved grant before signing another update.

### Place Orders

The Trader must have granted fee approval for the Builder before submitting
attributed orders. The order's Builder fee must be covered by that approval.
These examples place an immediate-or-cancel buy using an existing trading
session or signed order.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Call `session.placeOrder()` on the Trader's existing `PerpsSession`, opened
> with `builderAttribution`. The session uses the selected Builder and its saved
> approved fee. Set `instrumentId` to the instrument you want to trade:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { OrderSide, PerpsTimeInForce } from "@polymarket/client";
>
> const result = await session.placeOrder({
>   instrumentId,
>   side: OrderSide.BUY,
>   quantity: "0.01",
>   timeInForce: PerpsTimeInForce.IOC,
> });
> ```
>
> > [accordion] Output: PlacePerpsOrderResult

> > };
> >

> >   id: PerpsOrderId;
> >   instrumentId: PerpsInstrumentId;
> >   side: OrderSide;
> >   price: DecimalString;
> >   quantity: DecimalString;
> >   timeInForce: PerpsTimeInForce;
> >   postOnly: boolean;
> >   reduceOnly: boolean;
> >   status: PerpsOrderStatus;

> >   filledQuantity: DecimalString;

> >   updatedTimestamp: EpochMilliseconds;

> >   tpSl: PerpsTpSlOrderFields | undefined;

> >   feeRate: DecimalString;
> > };
> > ```

> [tab] API
>
> Submit a signed `createOrders` operation with the Builder's account address and

> from the quickstart above. Replace the sample salt and timestamp with fresh
> values, then submit the exact operation, salt, and timestamp that you signed:
>
> ```bash Request theme={null}

>           "buy": true,

>           "tif": "ioc",
>           "po": false,
>           "c": "7f9e4a2b6c8d0e1f1234567890abcdef",
>           "builder": {
>             "address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>             "fee_rate": "<builder_fee_rate>"
>           }
>         }
>       ]
>     },
>     "sig": "<order_signature>",
>     "salt": 234567890,
>     "ts": 1767000010000
>   }'
> ```
>
> ```ts OrderResponse Type theme={null}
> type OrderResponse = {
>   status: "ok";
>   oid: number;
>   coid?: string;
>   builder?: {
>     address: string;
>     fee_rate: string;
>   };
> } | {

>   error: string;
>   oid?: number;
>   coid?: string;
> };
> ```
>
> ```json OrderResponse Example theme={null}
> [
>   {
>     "status": "ok",
>     "oid": 67890,
>     "coid": "7f9e4a2b6c8d0e1f1234567890abcdef",
>     "builder": {
>       "address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234",
>       "fee_rate": "0.001"
>     }
>   }
> ]
> ```
>
> Check each result in the response array. `status: "ok"` confirms acceptance and
> `oid` identifies the order. `status: "err"` includes the rejection in `error`.
> Acceptance does not confirm execution. Read the order state or follow private
> order updates to determine the execution outcome.

### Display Trader Fees

Show the total fee charged for each execution, with exchange and Builder fees
as the breakdown. A maker rebate can make the total negative. Do not clamp it
to zero.

> [tab] TypeScript
>
> Read fills with `session.listFills()` on the Trader's `PerpsSession`:
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> const pages = session.listFills();
> const page = await pages.firstPage();
> const fills = page.items;
> ```
>
> Each item in `fills` has this shape. Use `totalFee` to display the total charge.
>
> > [accordion] Output: PerpsAccountFill
> >

> >   tradeId: PerpsTradeId;
> >   orderId: PerpsOrderId;
